title: "I Don't Care Who You Are": Baker Mayfield Gets Real on Replacing Tom Brady as Buccaneers QB
description: Baker Mayfield has never had any real chance of escaping the Tom Brady comparisons in Tampa Bay. Brady left the Buccaneers after the 2022 season as a seven-time Super Bowl champion, and Mayfield arrived the following year with the unenviable job of taking over at quarterback.
fullText:
Baker Mayfield has never had any real chance of escaping the Tom Brady comparisons in Tampa Bay. Brady left the Buccaneers after the 2022 season as a seven-time Super Bowl champion, and Mayfield arrived the following year with the unenviable job of taking over at quarterback.

More than three years later, Mayfield still understands why people make the comparison. But speaking to former Buccaneers stars Jarvis Landry and Leonard Fournette on 4th & South, he made it clear that trying to become the next Brady was never on his agenda.

"I've always been me," he said. "You can never replace Tom Brady's shoes. I don't care who you are. Only thing I can do is come in and be the best version of me. And that's talking s–t, making sure that I lead in the way I know how to lead and just be myself. Not try and do it the way he did, 'cause, I mean, he was 40 something at that stage. I mean he probably knew what a defense was doing before they broke the huddle.

The standard Brady left behind was enormous. He spent three seasons with Tampa Bay, winning Super Bowl LV in his first year with the franchise and taking the Buccaneers to the playoffs in every single season. Anybody who replaced Brady would be subjected to the same level of scrutiny that Mayfield faced.

Baker Mayfield isn't backing down from the biggest shoes in NFL history. 

Mayfield might not have been perceived as a franchise quarterback when the Buccaneers first signed him. It was foolish to expect him to do what Brady did, and Mayfield came to Tampa Bay after stints at Cleveland, Carolina, and Los Angeles. The quarterback was initially signed for only one year. But after debuting with a 9-8 record as a Buccaneer, Mayfield earned his place.

Today, the Bucs have been to two postseasons with him as the starting quarterback.

So when the Brady comparisons come up, Mayfield is not really engaging with them. He has his own resume to point to now, and that seems to be exactly where his head is at.

He is locked into a long-term three-year, $100 million contract that keeps him in Tampa Bay through the 2026 season. Mayfield's job is to build something of his own, and after more than three seasons in the role, he seems comfortable with that distinction. He is hoping to sign a new extension with the Buccaneers, although contract negotiations have been "disappointing" for him. However, Mayfield definitely deserves to be the franchise quarterback he knows he can be for Tampa Bay.

title: Faceoff! Ian Machado Garry doesn’t quite tower over Islam Makhachev in front of Philly’s Rocky statue
description: The UFC returns to the ‘City of Brotherly Love’ this Saturday, August 15th for UFC 330, and they’re using some of the most iconic backdrops from Philadelphia to help promote its fights. On Tuesday we got to see the title fight participants square off for the first time in front of Philly’s historic Rocky statue […]
fullText:
The UFC returns to the 'City of Brotherly Love' this Saturday, August 15th for UFC 330, and they're using some of the most iconic backdrops from Philadelphia to help promote its fights.

On Tuesday we got to see the title fight participants square off for the first time in front of Philly's historic Rocky statue outside of the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Islam Makhachev will defend his welterweight title (and attempt to surpass Anderson Silva's record for most consecutive wins in a row) when he takes on Ian Machado Garry. In the co-main, Mackenzie Dern will defend her women's strawweight title for the first time against Canadian submission expert Gillian Robertson.

One thing that has been brought up time and time again leading into the fight between Makhachev and Garry is the supposed size difference. Makhachev had spent the first 15 years of his MMA career at 155 pounds, moving up to 170 to take the belt off Jack Della Maddalena at UFC 322. He had no problem dealing with Della Maddalena, but there have been questions regarding Ian Machado Garry being much bigger.

A career-defining clash 👊@MAKHACHEVMMA vs @iangarryMMA 

[ #UFC330 | LIVE SAT AUG 15 | 9pmET on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/LIs18fqJWq

For Strawweight dominance 😤@MackenzieDern vs @savage_ufc 

[ #UFC330 | LIVE SAT AUG 15 | 9pmET on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/ZvccqIPjts

Garry is listed as 6 foot 3 inches on UFC.com, while Makhachev is just 5 foot 10 inches. Graphic mock-ups from fans on the internet had Garry portrayed as a behemoth next to the runty Makhachev. But today's faceoff in front of the Rocky statue tells a different story. Sure, Garry is a bit taller. But the size difference is not looking as significant as advertised.

Does this change Garry's chances of beating Makhachev? Makhachev was already the favorite coming into Philly, but he may get a few more bets placed on him coming into the final days of fight week. Even if he beats Garry with the same ease as he manhandled JDM, we expect there to always be whispers that the former lightweight can't handle the latest big welterweight.

All will be revealed when Makhachev and Garry finally step into the cage on Saturday night.

title: Rohit Sharma's Bollywood connection: John Abraham reveals surprise cricket link to former India captain
description: John Abraham revealed how Rohit Sharma has a unique connection to the film fraternity.
fullText:
Bollywood actor John Abraham surprised many when he revealed former India captain Rohit Sharma's surprising connection to the film star.

During the jersey launch event for Rotterdam Dockers held in Mumbai, ahead of the inaugural European T20 Premier League, Abraham was spotted alongside Dinesh Lad, Rohit's childhood batting coach.

Lad, who attended the event, posed for photographs with Abraham, which prompted the actor to bring the cat out of the bag for waiting journalists.

Abraham, who serves as one of the franchise's co-owners, alongside Jonty Rhodes, Faf du Plessis and Heinrich Klaasen, said: "He is Rohit Sharma's batting coach. He was my coach too. This is my gurudakshina to him."

The co-owner of Indian Super League side NorthEast United further revealed he had trained under Lad for roughly four months during his childhood.

"A lot of people look at me as just an actor. He enjoyed my cover drive," he said.

Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source

Rohit Sharma's childhood coach is Dinesh Lad, who spotted him when the batsman was just 12 years old.

"I first saw him as a bowler; he was about 12 years old. I saw him playing a match against us. Then I told his uncle (Chacha) to get him admitted to my school," Lad had said earlier on a podcast with Gaurav Mangalani.

"The school started in 1995, and I saw Rohit in 1999. He took admission that year. In the first year, he was in under 14. During practice, I kept making him bowl. Next year, Rohit went to 8th standard and was 14 years old."

Lad further revealed how he discovered Rohit's batting prowess while the youngster was hitting it out in the nets.

"One day, while entering the school, I saw a boy knocking (batting). From outside, I saw the bat was coming very straight and good," he added.

"I didn't know it was Rohit at first. When I went inside, I asked him if he was batting. He said yes, sir. Then I gave him some batting in the nets at number six or seven. Before that, I had never given him batting practice. That was my mistake."

Rohit Sharma is preparing to step into an entirely new arena, making his television debut through a brand-new entertainment show set to air on Sony.

It has been reported that it will be an Indian version of the American show Family Feud. There will be 40 episodes of one hour each.

News of the project first surfaced in May 2026 through a viral promotional teaser that saw Rohit say, "Koi bhi garden mein nahi ghumega."

title: Nick Lodolo Returns With New Curveball Grip as Reds Rally Past White Sox
description: Overcoming a recurring blister and a four-run deficit, Cincinnati’s southpaw debuted a revamped breaking ball to anchor a thrilling extra-innings comeback fueled by a dominant bullpen performance.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Reds bounced back with a series-opening win over the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday, August 11. The Reds came back from a 4-0 deficit and won 5-4 in extra innings, using big offensive moments from Eugenio Suarez, Tyler Stephenson, and Elly De La Cruz to seal the victory.

Nick Lodolo got his first start in the month of August after spending an extended amount of time on the IL with a blister issue. He was activated from the IL after one rehab start with the Louisville Bats. It's the second time this season he's missed time with the blister on his left index finger, which usually flares up after repeated use of his curveball.

Lodolo experimented with a new grip on his curveball during his most recent IL stint. That decision obviously raises questions about how the pitch's effectiveness may be affected by such a massive change. However, Lodolo's instant return on the grip change didn't result in any deficiencies, as it seemed as impactful as ever.

"It felt good; I thought I was able to throw it for a strike a lot," Lodolo said. "Obviously, there are different steps with that I want to get to. But overall, I was happy with how it felt, and the result with that pitch was pretty solid. So, definitely something to build off of."

The former first-round pick threw 70 pitches in four innings of work and allowed four earned runs on three home runs by the White Sox.

He threw his curveball 24 times, five more times than the next-most-thrown pitch, which was his sinker. Zach Sweet of MLB.com says Lodolo registered three of his five strikeouts using his curveball as his putaway pitch.

Lodolo gave up a first-inning home run to Brenton Doyle, a second-inning home run to Edgar Quero, and a fourth-inning home run to Miguel Vargas. Sam Antonacci doubled in the fourth; Randal Grichuk scored to give the White Sox a 4-0 lead.

While there is a lot to work on from a command standpoint, Lodolo threw 46 strikes in 70 pitches, 34 of which were in the strike zone, and left some pitches over the plate that Chicago punished; he gave the Reds a chance to win and kept the offense within striking distance after leaving the game in the fourth.

The bullpen came through in the final six innings of the game. Luis Mey threw two innings of scoreless ball. Pierce Johnson, Tejay Antone, and Brock Burke each threw up a zero in their single inning of work as well. Emilio Pagan came in the 10th following Elly De La Cruz's sacrifice fly and recorded the save, which included a 14-pitch strikeout of Sam Antonacci to open the inning.

Lodolo's main goal for the rest of the season should be to remain healthy, as the Reds pitching staff is going through enough injuries at the moment.

title: Marco Sturm Faces Bigger Bruins Challenge After Remarkable Debut
description: Marco Sturm exceeded expectations in his first season with the Bruins, but Year 2 will bring an even greater challenge.
fullText:
Marco Sturm Faces Bigger Bruins Challenge After Remarkable Debut originally appeared on NESN. 

Marco Sturm gave the Boston Bruins nearly everything they could have reasonably expected during his first season behind an NHL bench.

His reward will be significantly greater expectations in Year 2.

Sturm inherited a team coming off a last-place finish in the Atlantic Division and immediately restored its identity. Boston finished 45-27-10, reached 100 points and returned to the Stanley Cup playoffs after a one-year absence. The Bruins ultimately lost their first-round series against the Buffalo Sabres in six games, leaving a disappointing conclusion attached to an otherwise encouraging season. Still, Sturm's debut proved he could handle the pressure of coaching in Boston while implementing a new system and developing several important young players.

That was enough to make his first season successful.

Repeating it will be considerably harder.

"We're not going to be a surprise team anymore," Sturm said during Boston's end-of-season media availability. "That's why it's going to be really important how we come out of the gate."

Sturm has identified the challenge. Now he must help the Bruins meet it.

Sturm arrived with a clear vision for how he wanted Boston to play. The former Bruins forward emphasized defensive responsibility, quick transitions, offensive urgency and physicality. His players embraced that approach, giving Boston an identity that had been missing during its disappointing 2024-25 campaign.

General manager Don Sweeney credited Sturm with successfully navigating the demands of his first NHL head-coaching job.

"The coaches obviously did a really, really commendable job," Sweeney said. "Really proud of Marco in terms of all the things he was faced with, challenges and realizing how much greater is on his plate as a head coach. And he navigated it pretty well."

The Bruins were structured defensively, difficult to play against and committed to working as a five-man unit. Jeremy Swayman also rebounded from a difficult season and emerged as a Vezina Trophy finalist, giving Sturm the elite goaltending required to make his system work.

Boston's 100-point finish exceeded outside expectations, especially after the organization had traded Brad Marchand, Charlie Coyle, Brandon Carlo and Trent Frederic during the previous season.

Sturm did more than simply stabilize the Bruins. He convinced them they could win again.

The standard changes in Sturm's second season. Returning to the playoffs was a meaningful accomplishment in Year 1. Another first-round exit would be far more difficult to celebrate in Year 2.

Buffalo exposed several areas Boston must improve. The Bruins struggled to generate offense around the net and failed to consistently reach the difficult scoring areas that become even more important during the postseason.

"What I really noticed is if you look around the playoffs now, how goals get scored, everything is in the paint," Sturm said after Boston's Game 6 loss. "For some reason, we didn't get there."

That observation should influence how Sturm approaches his second season.

David Pastrnak remains the offensive centerpiece, but Boston cannot depend on its superstar winger to carry the scoring burden every night. Sturm must find dependable line combinations, create more offense from the middle of the lineup and ensure the Bruins can produce when opponents limit Pastrnak.

Boston also needs to avoid becoming overly reliant on Swayman. Elite goaltending can cover flaws throughout the regular season, but the Bruins must become a more complete team if they expect to survive multiple playoff rounds.

Sturm's work with Boston's younger players was one of the most promising aspects of his debut season. Fraser Minten played all 82 games as a rookie and finished with 17 goals and 35 points. He began the season in a bottom-six role before earning opportunities as Boston's second-line and even first-line center.

Marat Khusnutdinov recorded 15 goals and 33 points before ending the season alongside Pastrnak and Pavel Zacha on the top line. James Hagens also reached the NHL late in the season. The young center recorded one assist in two regular-season appearances and played three postseason games after beginning the year at Boston College.

Sturm showed he was willing to reward young players instead of restricting them to predetermined roles. That must continue. Minten needs to prove his rookie production was the beginning of something larger. Khusnutdinov must establish himself as a consistent top-six option, while Hagens could force his way into a much more prominent role.

Their development could determine whether the Bruins merely remain competitive or take a legitimate step toward Stanley Cup contention.

MORE: Charlie McAvoy's Top-10 Snub Sends Clear Message to Bruins Star

Sturm no longer is the new coach attempting to repair a struggling team. He is now the coach of a 100-point club expected to build upon its surprising success.

The Bruins should be more comfortable in his system, and Sturm should have a better understanding of how to manage an NHL season. That familiarity removes some of the natural excuses attached to a first-year coach.

There also is the question of how Boston responds when adversity arrives. The Bruins will not sneak up on opponents this season, and a difficult stretch could test whether Sturm's message remains as effective the second time around.

His first season created belief and restored pride in Boston.

His second will reveal whether the Bruins' resurgence was the beginning of something sustainable or simply one impressive year that arrived ahead of schedule.

title: Sean Payton reacts to Teddy Bridgewater’s retirement: ‘Proud of him’
description: "He was a great asset, a really, really good teammate," Broncos coach Sean Payton said of retiring quarterback Teddy Bridgewater.
fullText:
Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton sure has had an eventful last week when it comes to players he coached with the New Orleans Saints.

Payton participated at the enshrinement of Pro Football Hall of Famer Drew Brees on Saturday, and now, another former quarterback, Teddy Bridgewater, announced his retirement from the NFL on Monday.

Payton spoke highly of Bridgewater, who was with the Saints from 2018-19. "Our experience, my experience was fantastic," Payton said after Tuesday's practice. "I sent him a text last night... I saw the same news you guys did, and then it seemed to be more finalized. He was getting on a bus to play a preseason game I think, and we made a trade for him. I know I was at our Touchdown Club banquet like we have here. He was a great asset, a really, really good teammate. He had some rare leadership skills."

Payton knew Bridgewater's role with New Orleans was truly lasting in its impact. "He was important," Payton said. "He was on our team during a ton of wins. When Drew (Brees) got hurt (in 2019), he went 5-0."

Bridgewater also spent the 2021 season in Denver, playing in 14 games, going 7-7 as a starter. He threw for 3,052 yards, scored 20 total touchdowns (18 passing, two rushing) and tossed seven interceptions as a Broncos starter.

Football will likely always be in Bridgewater's DNA. "I think he'll find his way back into coaching or some role with football," Payton said. "So proud of him."

In the meantime, it's back to business in the NFL. The Broncos will have one final practice (closed to the public) on Wednesday before departing to Georgia, where they will face the Atlanta Falcons in their first preseason contest on Friday.

title: Clubs placed under transfer embargoes reassure fans
description: AFC Fylde and FC Halifax Town insist there are no financial problems at the National League clubs after being handed temporary transfer embargoes.
fullText:
AFC Fylde and Halifax Town have moved to reassure supporters there are no financial problems at the National League clubs after they were two of six teams placed under a temporary transfer embargo.

Aldershot Town, Hornchurch and Morecambe and Altrincham were also sanctioned on Tuesday over non-compliance with the league's financial regulations following late submission of budgetary information.

Altrincham's ban was lifted on Wednesday morning after the relevant paperwork was supplied and Fylde and Halifax have issued statements to confirm they are confident of a similar outcome.

"Following confirmation that AFC Fylde has been placed under a temporary transfer embargo by the National League, the club would like to reassure supporters that this relates solely to the late submission of financial information," read a Fylde statement.

"This is purely an administrative matter and does not relate to the financial position of the club. We fully expect this matter to be resolved shortly and swiftly."

Halifax have told the league they will supply the relevant information by the start of next week.

"We would like to clarify the situation to put people's minds at rest," the club said in a statement.

"The situation is very temporary and relates to the submission of some financial budgetary information. Our information is being submitted late for reasons explained to the National League on Monday where a further extension was requested until Monday 17th August.

"They have their League rules and have chosen to go down this particular route. We fully expect to have our information submitted as described.

"We must stress it has nothing to do with the actual finances of the football club. Everything is in good shape in that respect. It is purely administrative."

Aldershot, Hornchurch and Morecambe have yet to comment publicly.

title: 2026 St. Jude Championship Preview, Full Field And Odds
description: Taking a look and previewing the field, purse, picks, and predictions for the first leg of the FedEx Cup Playoffs, the St. Jude Championship.
fullText:
The 2026 FedEx Cup Playoffs are here, and the first leg of the playoffs starts with the FedEx St. Jude Championship. Unlike full field tournaments, the PGA Tour has created a unique final stretch run for the game's best players.

For the St. Jude Championship the top 70 players make the field. It is a no cut event, but only the top 50 will qualify for the second leg, the BMW Championship next week. After that tournament only the top 30 qualify for the Tour Championship at East Lake.

It all starts with the St. Jude Championship, and you'll see the best players in the game in the field this week. It might not have the feel of a major tournament, but it will certainly be worth watching.

Let's take a look at the details of the upcoming St. Jude Championship:

Course Details: Par 70, 7,288 yards

Field: St. Jude Championship Field

It's still important to take a look at the past winners of this event:

Let's take a look at pre-tournament winner odds:

When it comes to picks for this event, I'd start with my favorite and long shot picks. The favorite pick is the winner pick I like the most. For the long shot winner, that is a golfer who has over +2000 odds to win. It is a long shot pick for a reason, and finding those can be like finding a needle in a haystack.

Here are my favorite and long shot picks for the 2026 St. Jude Championship:

Favorite: Scottie Scheffler (+450)

Long Shot: Viktor Hovland (+3600)

I've said this a lot this season in these prediction articles, but I stand by it. Scottie Scheffler is too good to not win more tournaments. Unfortunately, Scheffler is running out of time, and only has one tournament win to his record this season. I believe Scheffler will be able to claim victory at some point during the FedEx Cup Playoffs, and why not at the St. Jude?

My long shot play at one time was an educated guess as to who might perform well on that specific course, etc. However, I'm turning this into a "gut pick". This tournament has often been won by a lesser-known player, and I'll go with Viktor Hovland this week as my long shot play.

Depending on how Rory McIlroy plays at TPC Southwind, I may or may not stay away from him outside of majors. It makes you wonder if Rory is now a "majors only" type golfer who doesn't have the desire to play, and win, these lesser tournaments on the schedule. We'll see how he does in Memphis.

If Scheffler doesn't win, it is a safe bet he'll be near the top of the leaderboard. I don't like negative odds in golf betting, but I'll take Scottie Scheffler at -106, nearly even odds, in a way to hedge our outright victory prediction.

It feels as if Morikawa is finally healthy, and starting to play at the level most expected of him when the year began. Morikawa, when he's on his game, is one of the game's best players, so getting +200 for a Top 10 finish with a limited field felt like an easy pick.

I've been weary of betting Aberg since his collapse at the Players Championship earlier this year, but I have a hunch Ludvig will return to form. I'm not asking for an outright win, but just a Top 10 finish. We haven't seen Aberg in a couple weeks, so hopefully he is rested and back on top of his game.

I was rather surprised when I saw Wyndham Clark getting +132 odds for a Top 20 finish. Clark, while struggling after the Open Championship, is still one of the better players on tour this year, so I felt it was an easy pick to make. Hopefully Clark gets back to his winning ways.

My "gut pick" of the week, outside of the long shot play, is Rickie Fowler. Fowler has slowly put his game back together and qualified for the FedEx Cup Playoffs. Fowler has been playing great golf, and a top 20 finish at +150 felt like a smart play in this limited field event.

For bonus plays, these are picks which I don't necessarily hang my hat on, but still provide value for some who want more exotic plays outside of the aforementioned picks. Sometimes bonus plays are parlays, double chances, triple chances, and even some fun plays for that particular event.

Here are the bonus plays for the 2026 St. Jude Championship:

Big Guns (+110) vs. the Field: Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young, Xander Schauffele, Tommy Fleetwood, Sam Burns, Matt Fitzpatrick, Ludvig Aberg to win

Margin of Victory: 2 Shots (+355)

title: Neto attracting Premier League interest
description: Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City.  The 26-year-old Portugal international is not regarded as one of the 'untouchable' players at Stamford Bridge and could therefore move before the transfer deadline.  The club believe the market for wide forwards has been inflated by a lack of options for leading clubs, highlighted by the £117m fee paid for Morgan Rogers and Paris St-Germain's £145m valuation of Bradley Barcola.
fullText:
Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City.

The 26-year-old Portugal international is not regarded as one of the 'untouchable' players at Stamford Bridge and could therefore move before the transfer deadline.

However, Chelsea insist they would demand a significant fee for the attacker, who joined from Wolves for £54m in 2024.

The club believe the market for wide forwards has been inflated by a lack of options for leading clubs, highlighted by the £117m fee paid for Morgan Rogers and Paris St-Germain's £145m valuation of Bradley Barcola.

Those figures have influenced Chelsea's valuation of Neto, who is known to be of interest to Manchester City where he would be reunited with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca.

Maresca and Neto are understood to have a strong relationship, and the winger is among those reported to have been frustrated by the Italian's departure midway through last season.

New manager Xabi Alonso has not commented on Neto's future, but he has played the winger in pre-season friendlies, including the 3-0 win over AC Milan on Saturday.

title: Köln to release El Mala if Dortmund submit €55m bid as AC Milan wait in wings
description: If Borussia Dortmund submits the reported €55million offer for said El Mala, 1.FC Köln, will apparently release the player from the club. According to the Express, sporting director Thomas Kessler...
fullText:
If Borussia Dortmund submits the reported €55million offer for said El Mala, 1.FC Köln, will apparently release the player from the club.

According to the Express, sporting director Thomas Kessler has made this promise to El Mala and his representatives.

However, those close to the club in Köln are apparently unsure whether Borussia Dortmund can even afford such an offer.

"The offers received so far have been so low that some are saying Dortmund simply doesn't have the required €50million available," the tabloid reported.

El Mala remains Dortmund's absolute top target. The talented left winger also wants to join the German runners-up and has already agreed to a five-year contract.

Only the agreement with Cologne is still pending, but this is expected to be achieved through the new offer.

Meanwhile, another interested party is lurking in the background, with the Express suggesting AC Milan intends to make a move if BVB fails.

title: Latest NHL contract trend is a smart move for the players
description: NHL players and front offices are getting smarter with their contracts.
fullText:
NHL general managers have been giving out shorter-term contracts with higher per-season pay. Is this the new strategy? GMs giving fewer years on contracts means more leverage for the team.

Giving players more money and fewer years allows teams to trade them if they need to move off a contract. Recently, Connor McDavid signed a two-year contract with an annual value of $12.5 million. Of course, more money per season is a win for the players.

MORE: NHL players facing the most pressure entering 2026-2027 season

Edmonton Oilers forward Connor McDavid (97) during a game at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images

Short-term contracts help the team more than the players because the teams have the leverage in the situation. The Oilers are signing Connor McDavid to a short-term contract, which puts the team in a better position with their salary cap.

Signing their top superstars can get them into injury trouble if it's long-term. And if you sign one of your stars to a six-year deal, then teams have to worry about their future contracts with that one contract in the way.

If the San Jose Sharks signed Macklin Celebrini to a seven-year deal, I think there is more of a reward than risk because the production is there, the Sharks have a young nucleus in Celebrini, and they can become a great team in the West. His contract now is still great, with him being on a five-year contract worth $94 million.

MORE: 5 NHL teams that will surprise in 2026-2027

Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Penguins right wing Ville Koivunen (41) passes the puck against the Washington Capitals during the third period at PPG Paints Arena. Mandatory Credit: Philip G. Pavely-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Recently, a few players got luxurious deals, such as Alex Tuch, Ville Koivunen, and Darren Raddysh; these contracts have risks. Alex Tuch is 30 years old and signed an eight-year deal. He has put up strong numbers, but it comes with risks because, with him aging, there is more injury risk or concern.

Smaller terms can make sense because you want to keep all of your elite players. A shorter deal gives the players another chance to hit the market and negotiate a bigger contract while they're in their prime years.

Players often take risks by signing shorter contracts. By agreeing to a smaller deal, they can potentially increase their earnings if they perform exceptionally well over two years. This strategy allows them to elevate their contract value from eight million per season to twelve million, capitalizing on their peak performance years.

More flexibility for both sides is important. Players tend to leverage themselves, and teams try it too. Keeping it balanced helps players get another opportunity if things don't cash in, or the team gets flexibility if things don't work out.

title: Johansson on statement signing Hodge, HJK and 'playing our way'
description: Manager Alfred Johansson has been speaking to the media before Motherwell face HJK in the second leg of their Conference League third-round qualifier.  Johansson is "absolutely buzzing" to bring "very exciting" midfielder Joe Hodge to the club.  Despite bringing in large transfer fees over the course of the past year, Johansson says Motherwell are "still going to be strategic" with incomings but agrees that Hodge's arrival signals real ambition by the club, given the pedigree he arrives with.
fullText:
Manager Alfred Johansson has been speaking to the media before Motherwell face HJK in the second leg of their Conference League third-round qualifier.

Johansson is "absolutely buzzing" to bring "very exciting" midfielder Joe Hodge to the club. The manager says he is "mainly a number six in our system" but can also have a "more box-to-box" role.

The Swedish coach says the Republic of Ireland international possesses the "vision, quality on the ball and mobility" to play at the base of his side's midfield.

Despite bringing in large transfer fees over the course of the past year, Johansson says Motherwell are "still going to be strategic" with incomings but agrees that Hodge's arrival signals real ambition by the club, given the pedigree he arrives with.

Hodge will not be eligible for Motherwell's match with HJK on Thursday, while left-sided defender Dylan Williams still faces another "week or two" on the sidelines.

Strikers Eythor Bjorgolfsson and Apostolos Stamatelopoulos are back in training but are still doing individual work away from the team.

Johansson adds that his players will need a "strong, strong performance" to progress on Thursday following a 1-1 draw last week.

The Swede hailed his side's second-half display in Helsinki, saying they were "more fearless, more aggressive and that's us". "We want to excite, we want to play our way," he adds.

title: Nick Sirianni explains why Willie Lampkin continues to stand out
description: Willie Lampkin's size will always attract attention, but Nick Sirianni believes what he offers goes beyond what's on his scouting report.
fullText:
If Willie Lampkin walked into a room, most people would probably assume he's an athlete. What they might not assume is that he's competing for a spot on the Philadelphia Eagles' roster as part of one of the NFL's most physically imposing offensive lines.

That's understandable. The Eagles employ giants up front. Lane Johnson stands 6-foot-6. Jordan Mailata is 6-foot-8. Even Cam Jurgens, at 6-foot-3 and 303 pounds, is considered relatively modest by offensive line standards.

Then there's Lampkin. The former undrafted free agent measures 5-foot-11 and weighs roughly 279 pounds. On paper, those measurements seem better suited for an AAU basketball roster than life in the trenches against some of the biggest and strongest athletes in professional sports.

And yet, the Eagles continue giving him opportunities. Wouldn't you know it? He is making the most of them. That's because football evaluations don't begin and end with height and weight. Scouts can measure arm length, hand size and athletic testing numbers. What they can't fully measure is how a player responds to adversity, handles pressure or competes when facing longer, stronger opponents every day.

Lampkin has spent training camp answering every question asked about him in the best way possible. He has done so by performing. Lampkin has quietly put together an impressive summer.

Whether working at center or guard, he's shown the technical refinement, footwork and competitiveness that initially convinced Philadelphia he was worth developing. People inside and outside the organization have begun to notice. Head coach Nick Sirianni recently discussed what makes Lampkin stand out, and his answer centered less on physical traits and more on the qualities that often separate players who survive in the NFL from those who don't.

5'11" interior offensive lineman Willie Lampkin has been turning heads so far at Eagles training camp. pic.twitter.com/heSDzS7OPQ

That's important because concerns about Lampkin's size aren't imaginary. It would be easy to dismiss the conversation by asking, "If he's playing well, why does size matter?" The reality is that it does matter. Offensive linemen don't spend Sundays battling average athletes. They line up across from players like Leonard Williams, Jeffery Simmons and Quinnen Williams. All mentioned are on the Eagles' schedule this season.

That's life in the NFL. That's what Lampkin would have to endure if he makes the team and injuries forced him into action. If Aaron Donald ever decided to unretire, he'd be on that list, too. Lampkin will have to continue answering the questions. Seeing him play well vs. Jalen Carter and company certainly builds his confidence and the confidence coaches have in him.

The encouraging part for Philadelphia is that he hasn't looked overwhelmed by those concerns so far. Instead, he's continued stacking positive practices and forcing evaluators to focus on what he can do rather than what he lacks. That's often how long-shot offensive line projects carve out NFL careers.

Willie Lampkin may never look like a typical Eagles offensive lineman, and questions about his size probably aren't going away anytime soon. The good news for Philadelphia is that neither are the qualities Sirianni seems to value most. Lampkin competes, learns, and continues finding ways to win against longer and heavier opponents. That's why he's still in the conversation. In an organization that has built a reputation for developing overlooked talent, Lampkin is steadily making a case that he could be the next success story.

title: Countdown to kickoff: Recalling Trojans CB Christian Roland-Wallace

title: Barcelona youngster set to join Spanish club in €2-3 million permanent transfer
description: In an important development, Mundo Deportivo reports that FC Barcelona goalkeeper Áron Yaakobishvili, 20, is close to completing his move to UD Almeria. The Andalusian club will pay between €2 mill...
fullText:
In an important development, Mundo Deportivo reports that FC Barcelona goalkeeper Áron Yaakobishvili, 20, is close to completing his move to UD Almeria.

The Andalusian club will pay between €2 million and €3 million for the La Masia graduate, while Barça will retain 50–60% of the player's rights.

The Barcelona academy goalkeeper has chosen García Pimienta's project to get regular playing time and gain experience with a team that will be fighting to return to the top flight after last season's relegation.

As reported earlier this week, the Hungarian goalkeeper preferred to leave Barcelona rather than becoming the the third goalkeeper for the first team.

This leaves Hansi Flick with the option of choosing his third shot-stopper between Eder Aller and Iker Rodriguez, who is still a youth player, with the latter seeming to have the edge as things stand.

Iker Rodriguez will be the third-choice goalkeeper. (Photo courtesy: Instagram/@ikerrodriguez.01)

The two are expected to share goalkeeping duties for Barça Atletic alongside Max Bonfill, 19.

This season, the third-goalkeeper role will not be as fixed as it has been in previous years. Instead, the club plans to rotate them so they can all get competitive minutes with the reserve team.

Yaakobishvili took his time considering some of the first offers that arrived and began preseason with the first team after returning from his loan spell at Andorra, where he was a starter for a significant part of the season.

Set to join Almeria (Photo courtesy: X/@fcandorra)

A goalkeeper with quality and personality, the Hungarian came on in the second half of the friendly against Birmingham City and saved two penalties in the shootout, which Barcelona ultimately lost 3-2 on penalties.

The 20-year-old shot-stopper did not play in the triangular tournament in Udine last week.

If he had preferred to stay, the club would also have accepted that decision. But Yaakobishvili wants to play regularly and has decided to sign for Almeria.

The move to the Andalusian club will give him the opportunity to gain regular minutes and continue his development, while Barça will still retain some degree of control over his future.

title: ‘I don't know who made the decision’: Ex-India batter on Jasprit Bumrah's workload and CoE scrutiny
description: India's growing injury list has placed the Centre of Excellence under scrutiny. Several key players are currently dealing with various fitness issues and injuries. Jasprit Bumrah's knee swelling has led to his absence from the Sri Lanka Test series. Former batter Subramaniam Badrinath clarified the COE's role in providing player information. He stressed workload management and consistent monitoring are crucial for player fitness.
fullText:
India's growing injury list has put the Centre of Excellence (COE) under the spotlight, with several players across formats currently dealing with fitness issues.

Jasprit Bumrah is battling knee swelling, while Sai Sudharsan has been sidelined by a left big toe injury. Harshit Rana and Nitish Kumar Reddy are recovering from hamstring problems, while Washington Sundar is unavailable with a quadriceps injury.

The number of players missing or recovering from injuries has raised questions about India's injury management and rehabilitation system, particularly with the team preparing for an important phase across formats.

Bumrah's latest setback has attracted particular attention. The premier fast bowler has been ruled out of India's upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka after failing to recover from the knee injury he sustained during the England tour.

With Bumrah central to India's plans in all three formats, his fitness remains a major priority as the team looks towards the next World Cup and continues its campaign in the World Test Championship cycle.

The development has also led to scrutiny of the Centre of Excellence and its role in assessing players' fitness. However, former India batter Subramaniam Badrinath has stressed that the facility does not decide whether a player is selected.

According to Badrinath, the COE's responsibility is to provide the team management with information about a player's physical condition and recovery. The final decision on selection rests with the captain, coach and selectors.

"I don't know who made the decision. COE will not make the selection, right? They will just say he is in this state and can play these matches and his body is in this state. But I think the captain, coach, and selectors are taking the decision. COE only passes the information. They are not selectors," Subramaniam Badrinath said in a video on his YouTube channel.

Badrinath also urged caution against treating India's injury problems as a single issue. He pointed out that the players currently dealing with injuries have suffered different types of setbacks, making it difficult to identify one common cause behind the growing list.

While injuries are an inevitable part of elite sport, Badrinath believes workload management, fitness and consistent monitoring remain crucial to keeping players on the field.

"I don't have an immediate answer to the root cause of so many injuries. It is important to see what kind of injuries these are. At high-level professional sport, injuries are common. Sai Sudharsan got hit by a ball, with Bumah, it is a chronic injury because of being overused and fitness is not Sundar's forte, he is injury-prone. His fitness needs a lot of work. Management and monitoring is very important. Injuries are bound to happen and you cannot control it," he said.

The comments come at a time when India are having to manage the fitness of several important players, making rehabilitation and workload monitoring increasingly important as the team's schedule continues across formats.

title: Silver feels great for Azu after up-and-down year
description: Welsh sprinter Jeremiah Azu says it was "amazing" to help Great Britain claim a one-two in the 100m at the European Championships.
fullText:
Welsh sprinter Jeremiah Azu says it was "amazing" to be part of a Great Britain one-two in the European Championships 100m in Birmingham.

Englishman Romell Glave took gold in Tuesday's final at Alexander Stadium as he clocked 10.09, with Azu hitting the line in 10.16.

Success in the men's 100m came 24 hours after Great Britian's Amy Hunt won the women's event.

"Silver feels great," Azu told BBC One Breakfast. "Going into a championship, you always want to leave with a gold, but the gold going to a team-mate makes it better.

"We were able to do it together, but it's been an up-and-down year so to finish it off with a medal has been great."

GB's Glave and Azu claim European 100m one-two

GB's Hunt comes of age with European 100m gold

The team behind Hodgkinson's golden rise and the hunt for a world record

Azu, 25, said the Birmingham crowd "made it easy for us to perform".

"We get to race all over the world, but to have these special moments, these championships, they come quite rarely in your career so to have that opportunity was amazing, and I'm glad we could grasp it," he added.

"We did what we said we would do: take the gold and the silver in the 100m."

After becoming world and European champion over 60m indoors in 2025, Azu finished fourth at this year's World Indoor Championships and fifth at the Commonwealth Games, with a season's best of 10.00 in Glasgow two weeks ago not proving enough for a medal.

Second in Birmingham was reason for Azu to celebrate and he sent a message to a youth group he is involved with in home city Cardiff saying Wednesday's gathering was "cancelled".

Azu says helping youngsters is "a big passion", adding: "When I was that age, I didn't feel like I had anyone I could go to, so I want to just be that that sounding board for them because as much as I've been through, I'm not too far off their age.

"So it's like the experiences that they'll be going through, I understand.

"Just to be that person for them... hopefully they can look into what I'm doing and take inspiration from it, not just to pursue sports, but to give anything they want in life a real go, and you'd never know where it can take you."

Azu says his religious faith is also a significant factor in his life - including when he is waiting for the starting gun to fire.

"We put in hours and hours of training, so you have to stand on the start line, believing you're capable of it," he said.

"And especially for some of us, our faith is another thing that grounds us. We can stand there and know that it's not bigger than us.

"We've been given this talent so we can express ourselves confidently because we've got the combination of the hard work and the gift from God, so we can stand on that start line and not have any doubt."

title: European Championships: Day three schedule & BBC coverage
description: Timetable and BBC coverage times for the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham from 10-16 August.
fullText:
The first European Athletics Championships to be held in Great Britain are under way at Alexander Stadium in Birmingham.

The Championships take place from 10-16 August, with Britain's team of 94 athletes chasing top spot in the medals table.

Among the British stars on show are reigning 800m champion Keely Hodgkinson, Dina Asher-Smith, local boy Matthew Hudson-Smith, Katarina Johnson-Thompson, Amy Hunt, Georgia Hunter Bell and team captain Jake Wightman.

Global stars competing include Sweden's Armand Duplantis, Norway's Jakob Ingebrigtsen, Greece's Miltiadis Tentoglou, Italy's Marcell Jacobs, Ukraine's Yaroslava Mahuchikh and the Netherlands' Femke Broeders-Bol.

Athletes from 49 nations are competing for 50 gold medals - including a mixed 4x100m relay for the first time - and there are 10 world champions and seven Olympic champions taking part.

The BBC will bring you comprehensive coverage of the championships on BBC One, BBC Two, BBC iPlayer, Radio 5 Live, the BBC Sport website, the BBC Sport app and the BBC Sport social media channels including YouTube.

Hodgkinson & Asher-Smith in GB squad for Europeans

Sprinter Asher-Smith has won six European golds and two silvers from four championships and could overtake the record of seven golds to become the most successful athlete in the history of the competition.

Two athletes jointly hold that record - Croatian discus thrower Sandra Elkasevic (formerly Perkovic) and Jakob Ingebrigtsen, who picked up his seventh title with men's 5,000m victory on the opening night in Birmingham.

Asher-Smith finished sixth in her opening event, the women's 100m, but is expected to compete for two further medals - the women's 200m and either the mixed or women's 4x100m relay.

The 30-year-old could also draw level with fellow sprinter Irena Szewinska of Poland as the most-decorated European athlete of all time. Szewinska won a total of 10 medals from 1966-1978.

Of other current athletes, Dutch star Femke Broeders-Bol has five golds and a bronze from just two championships.

Hudson-Smith, who has a stand at Alexander Stadium named after him, has four golds and seven medals in total.

One more medal and he will equal France's Christophe Lamaitre as the championships' most-decorated male athlete of all-time.

A gold medal would also bring him level with Roger Black and Sir Mo Farah as the British men to have won most European titles.

The 31-year-old, who was born in Wolverhampton, competes in the men's 400m final on Wednesday evening and will have a further chance of winning a medal in the men's 4x400m relay on the final day.

Arguably the most-anticipated event for British fans is Hodgkinson's 800m battle with Audrey Werro and Femke Broeders-Bol.

Hodgkinson, 24, sat out the Commonwealth Games and comes into the championships after winning the London Diamond League meeting in July.

However, she faces two tough opponents in her quest for another title.

Swiss star Werro, 22, beat Hodgkinson in June and has twice run faster than the reigning Olympic champion this season, edging closer and closer to the 43-year-old world record of one minute 53.28 seconds.

Broeders-Bol, the 26-year-old world 400m hurdles champion, has moved up to 800m and finished just behind Hodgkinson at London Stadium as she makes rapid strides in her new event.

The women's 800m heats took place on Tuesday morning, the semi-finals are on Thursday morning at 12:10 and the final is at 21:45 on Friday, 14 August.

The team behind Hodgkinson's golden rise and the hunt for a world record

Why is the women's 800m record so tough to break?

Hunt is targeting a British record four gold medals at these championships in a bid to become "iconic".

The confident 24-year-old won 100m gold on Monday and is aiming to follow that up by winning the 200m title on Thursday, the women's 4x100m relay on Saturday and the inaugural mixed 4x100m relay on Sunday.

"Yes, I am looking to be iconic," she told BBC Sport. "I want to do what nobody has ever done before.

"I think this is the perfect place to do it. I am an East Midlands girl, and I am from Newark.

"This is the closest I am ever going to get to a home crowd in my entire career."

Team-mate Asher-Smith won three gold medals at the 2018 Europeans in Berlin.

You can watch live coverage of every session on either BBC One or BBC Two as well as iPlayer, the BBC Sport website and the BBC Sport app.

Radio 5 Live and BBC Sounds will be in Birmingham to bring you daily live commentary, while the BBC Sport website and app will feature live text, reports, analysis, video clips and a medal table.

There will also be coverage on BBC Sport's social media platforms, including YouTube.

Gabby Logan and Jeanette Kwakye will present the BBC TV coverage with Steve Cram, Andrew Cotter, Steve Backley, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe commentating on the action.

London 2012 Olympic champions Dame Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford plus Hodgkinson's coach Jenny Meadows will also provide analysis.

title: Bayonne now one win away from advancing to Little League World Series
description: Bayonne Little League is closing in on history, one win away from becoming the first Hudson County team to advance to the Little League World Series.
fullText:
Bayonne Little League is closing in on history.

With a win in Friday night's Metro Region championship game, the reigning New Jersey state champions would advance to the Little League World Series, becoming the first Hudson County team to accomplish the feat and first New Jersey charter since Toms River East did it in 2021.

Bayonne will face the winner of Game 5 between New York (PYA Port Washington) and Connecticut (Darien) in the Aug. 14 championship game. The New Jersey state champions have already secured a spot in the title matchup after opening the Metro Region tournament with convincing victories over Connecticut and New York.

Bayonne (13-0) won both its games this week in Bristol, Connecticut, outscoring its first two opponents, 20-4. The Bees have been dominant, opening with an 8-2 victory over Connecticut before overwhelming New York, 12-2, two days later.

More: Bayonne Little League in Metro Region: Scores, schedule, TV info

More: Get to know Bayonne Little League players as region tournament begins

In the win over New York, Mason Rincon set the tone early by blasting a two-run home run to center field. Later in the first inning, AJ Tapia lined a single down the right-field line to drive in two more runs, giving Bayonne a 4-0 lead after one inning.

Bayonne continued to pour on the offense, adding one run in the second inning, five 

Gabriel Garcia Jr. and Mason Rincon combined to pitch all four innings, with Garcia earning the victory. He worked the first two innings, allowing three hits and two earned runs while helping keep the Bees firmly in control. Rincon handled the final two innings as Bayonne closed out the 12-2 win under the run rule.

Since Bayonne has not played since Aug. 10, the team will have had several days to rest and prepare for the championship game.

Check out the photo gallery, then 

The winner of the tournament represents the region at the Little League World Series from Aug. 19-30 at the Little League International Complex, Lamade and Volunteer Stadiums in South Williamsport, Pennsylvania.

In the 78 years since the first Little League World Series tournament, only 20 New Jersey teams have qualified for the August classic. Toms River East (2021) is the last New Jersey team to reach a World Series and first since Elmora Youth (Elizabeth) in 2019.

Only four New Jersey teams – Hammonton (1949), Wayne American (1970), Lakewood (1975) and Tom River East American (1998) – have won Little League World Series titles.

Here's everything you need to know about for Friday's Metro Region championship game:

Matchup: New Jersey (Bayonne) vs. Game 5 winner between New York (PY A)/Connecticut (Darien).

Location: A. Bartlett Giamatti Little League Leadership Training Center, 335 Mix Street, Bristol, Connecticut.

Fans back home looking to catch Bayonne play can tune into ESPN for full coverage.

Weather has been a recurring factor in Bristol this week, with some games postponed and rescheduled because of intermittent rain. While additional inclement weather is expected in the area on Thursday, conditions are forecasted to improve significantly by Friday. Skies are expected to be clear and sunny, with temperatures around 65 degrees at game time.

Temperatures in Bristol have generally remained in the upper 70s to low 80s throughout the week.

title: Starting UNC guard shockingly transfers to different ACC school

title: Louisville adds North Carolina transfer G Seth Trimble
description: Seth Trimble, who spent the last four seasons playing key roles at North Carolina, is transferring to Louisville for his final year of college hoops. Trimble, who entered the transfer portal in the spring, became an option for Louisville to add after a Colorado district court ruling last month that gave Class of 2022 high […]
fullText:
Seth Trimble, who spent the last four seasons playing key roles at North Carolina, is transferring to Louisville for his final year of college hoops.

Trimble, who entered the transfer portal in the spring, became an option for Louisville to add after a Colorado district court ruling last month that gave Class of 2022 high schoolers an extra season of college eligibility.

As a "senior" in 2025-26, Trimble averaged 14.0 points and 3.0 assists per game for the Tar Heels. He scored a career-high 30 points in a win over Louisville. Perhaps most notably, Trimble hit the game-winning shot at the buzzer un UNC's upset of arch-rival Duke.

After going undrafted in June, Trimble averaged 10.8 ppg for the Washington Wizards in the NBA's Summer League. He did not, however, sign an official contract with the Wizards, a move which left the door open for him to return to college.

Known for his defensive prowess and ability to attack the rim than his outside shooting (28.6 percent from three last year), Trimble is an interesting add for a Louisville team that seemed to be more or less set in the backcourt. I suppose when you have the opportunity to add an experienced, All-ACC caliber performer, you take it regardless of your current situation.

One thing that Trimble absolutely adds that U of L may have been lacking is a knack for making the biggest play at the biggest moment. It's not just the Duke shot, either. Look at how many of the plays in this reel are game-saving, game-winning type plays.

Seth Trimble is a Louisville Cardinal! pic.twitter.com/FHrrBRufml

To quote Jeff Brohm, "all we can do right now is the use the current rules that are out there to the best of our advantage."

These are strange times, bit if you're standing still when you have the opportunity to move forward, you're basically moving backwards.

Now the big question will become whether or not PK and company are done with preseason acquisitions.

title: Caleb Williams Watch: How Bears QB fared on Day 12 of training camp
description: The Chicago Bears were back at Halas Hall for training camp on Tuesday. We're recapping Caleb Williams' outing on Day 12.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears were back at training camp on Tuesday for their 12th practice of the summer, and there was plenty to break down from Day 12, including the performance of quarterback Caleb Williams.

Williams is entering his third season following a breakout sophomore campaign where he set a franchise single-season passing record, led an NFL record seven fourth quarter comebacks (including the postseason) while leading Chicago to an 11-6 record, NFC North title and playoff win. That was all in one season with head coach Ben Johnson. Now, all eyes are on Williams this summer as he continues to develop under Johnson and make a huge leap in Year 3.

We're taking a look at the good, the bad and the noteworthy with Williams from the 12th practice of Bears training camp:

It wasn't a perfect day for Williams, but it was a strong day nonetheless. According to Chris Emma, Williams was "sharp" and the offensive operation was overall "crisp" on Tuesday. Clay Harbor noted that Williams made some nice throws. "During backed-up work, he created space and found Rome Odunze then Scotty Miller." Nicholas Moreano singled out one throw to Kalif Raymond on a screen pass that the veteran receiver took for a touchdown against the second-team defense. Overall, Williams has had an impressive two weeks of camp so far, where Chris Emma noted he's "showcased his command in Ben Johnson's offense."

For the most part, Williams and the offense had a solid showing. But it wasn't perfect. Both the first- and second-team offenses struggled during situational drills at the end of practice, according to Courtney Cronin, where Williams got rid of the ball on fourth-and-3.

The Bears offense had a relatively successful practice, including acing a tough test near the end of practice, per Courtney Cronin, where they were backed up at their own 1-yard line. "The goal for the drill was to get two first downs, which Williams accomplished by creating space to find Rome Odunze for a 50-plus yard catch-and-run followed by a big gain to Scotty Miller."

Through the first two weeks of training camp, Williams feels confident about where he's at and knows he can still improve.

"I just I want to keep getting better for the guys," Williams said. "I want to be faster with my process, to be able to help the O-line throughout you know long games and things like that, they're sitting in their stances, be able to get the communication throughout, you know whether it's on the ball or whether it's in the huddle, just be smoother and faster and everything so that I can be better for the guys and ultimately that helps us win."

title: How a Kanye West concert cost European football team Champions League qualification chances
description: A Kanye West concert has had a surprising impact on one football team that was trying to secure qualification for this season’s Champions League. While the proper tournament does not kick off until later this year, qualification for the league phase is already underway.
fullText:
A Kanye West concert has had a surprising impact on one football team that was trying to secure qualification for this season's Champions League.

While the proper tournament does not kick off until later this year, qualification for the league phase is already underway.

Among the teams who were trying to secure a spot in the league were Kairat Almaty, who made history back in 2025/26 when they became the first team from Kazakhstan to make it to the main draw.

However, they were not so fortunate this time around, losing a recent qualifying match which they had to play hundreds of miles from their home stadium due to a Kanye West concert.

Almaty were playing against Bulgarian outfit Levski Sofia, and went into the second leg needing to overturn a 1-0 deficit.

The first leg was played in Bulgaria, and the second game should, in turn, have taken place at Kairat's home stadium.

However, the Almaty Central Stadium has been booked by rapper Kanye for one of his comeback shows.

In turn, they had to face Levski Sofia at the Turkestan Arena, which is about 516 miles from their actual ground.

As a result, it was perhaps not surprising that without any real home advantage, they lost the second leg 1-0 and have been knocked out of the Champions League.

Almaty will now turn their attention back to the Kazakhstan Premier League, in which they are currently second.

They are four points off first place with a game in hand so they could still easily win the title this season.

But the extra revenue from making it into the Champions League's league phase could have been an even bigger boost for a team of that size.

title: Cal Raleigh gives blunt assessment of his performance with Mariners mired in losing streak: 'I'm awful'
description: Cal Raleigh provided some insight into why he believes the Mariners are struggling this year.
fullText:
One could argue Cal Raleigh was the story of the 2025 MLB season. Sure, Aaron Judge walked away with the American League MVP, but Raleigh was the breakout superstar. He clubbed 60 home runs, made his first All-Star team and won the Home Run Derby.

A year later, though, Raleigh is literally one of the worst hitters in the game. With the Mariners quickly falling out of the playoff hunt after losing their fifth-straight game, Raleigh surprised reporters by inviting an impromptu Q&A after Tuesday's 4-1 loss to the New York Yankees.

When asked about the team's current skid, Raleigh took the brunt of the responsibility, telling reporters, "I'm awful," per Ryan Divish of the Seattle Times.

"It's not good," he said. "We're not playing well. That starts with me. I'm awful. I've got to find a way to be better and to help bring the guys along. We just gotta play better. We're just playing very, very, very bad baseball in every facet of the game. We gotta pick it up — from the energy standpoint to the execution to the little things in the game that help you win baseball games. We're just not doing those things right now."

Raleigh then offered what appeared to be more insight into why he believes he's struggling at the plate, though his quotes could also be interpreted as him trying to send a message to his teammates. But he was careful to still shoulder the blame, adding, "I'm not pointing fingers. I'm ultimately the worst of the group right now, and I understand that."

"Sometimes baseball players can be stubborn, but we've just got to put our pride aside," he said. "We have to focus a little more on the team aspect, or hitting the ball the other way, or trying to just take singles and not trying to go for the long ball every time. Ultimately, when you rely on the long ball, you're gonna get a lot of off-balance swings and you're gonna be a little out front. The pitchers here are really good and you've got to take what they give you. We're just not doing that right now."

It's tough to overstate how much Raleigh has struggled coming off his near-MVP season. The 29-year-old is hitting just .159/.264/.299, with 12 home runs, through 86 games. He's also running the worst strikeout rate of his career since his brief debut year. Similarly, he's chasing pitches outside the zone with more frequency than any year except his first in the majors.

Raleigh isn't the only reason the Mariners have struggled in 2026. Injuries to key players have resulted in the team experiencing some lengthy absences from otherwise strong performers. First baseman Josh Naylor has mostly been healthy, but hasn't found his power stroke, and is slugging just .372 on the year.

Thanks to the team's recent slide, the Mariners enter Wednesday sitting at 56-64. Due to the mediocrity of the American League, the team is just four games out of a wild-card spot.

Despite its record, the team still has a chance to rally and make a playoff run. But any hope of that happening revolves around Raleigh and Co. finally finding their stride at the plate.

Raleigh delivered his message on what needs to change Tuesday. It's up to him and the rest of the Mariners to take it to heart and start producing.

title: What Scottie Scheffler said about Rory McIlroy’s pace of play during the playoffs in 2025
description: Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy have been paired together for the first time this season at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.
fullText:
Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy have been paired together for the first time this season at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

The last time Scheffler and McIlroy were drawn together was at the Tour Championship in August last year.

Interestingly, the American and the Northern Irishman were paired together the previous week as well, at the BMW Championship.

Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy have not played alongside each other so far in 2026, but that will change this week at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

Golf fans are seriously excited at the prospect of seeing the two best golfers in the world in the same group.

Scheffler and McIlroy have huge respect for one another, but they will both be desperate to beat each other this week at TPC Southwind.

Scheffler got the better of McIlroy when they played together at the BMW Championship last year.

The world number one went on to win that week at Caves Valley, while the Northern Irishman ended up in a tie for 12th.

After the opening round, Scheffler was asked how he found McIlroy's pace of play.

"Yeah, it's always fun playing with Rory, we draw a nice crowd," the 30-year-old said.

"The crowd did a great job of cheering us both on.

"He's a great pairing. He plays fast, he plays well and we had a good time out there."

McIlroy spoke about Scheffler's pace of play after they were paired together at the BMW Championship last year.

"I love playing with Scottie. I always have," said McIlroy.

"I like the cadence that he plays the game at. I like his rhythm. He doesn't really take a ton of time.

"I feel like there's guys that you like to get paired with, and there's guys – some guys that you don't. I've always enjoyed playing with Scottie."

Judging by those comments, Scheffler and McIlroy will surely be happy that they've been drawn to play together at the FedEx St. Jude Championship this week.

title: Na'eem Offord making 'night and day' improvement for Oregon
description: Na'eem Offord is making a big leap in his second fall camp with the Ducks.
fullText:
Cornerback is a deep position in Eugene this fall, with plenty of returning and new talent making some noise in fall camp. The Oregon Ducks have a plethora of options to turn to on the perimeter defensively, and the increasing intensity in practice is giving some of the young depth in the room a chance to show how far they've come.

Na'eem Offord is proving to be a big riser for the Ducks entering year two. The former five-star rotated in and appeared in every game last season for the Ducks as a freshman, but his inexperience showed. Now, with an offseason in the program under his belt, the defense isn't as complicated to Offord as it once was.

"It was just a learning experience," Offord said on Tuesday. "It's okay to sit back and learn from others and see what their preparation is. You know, the speed was way faster transferring (from) high school, so you know it was just a process. I had to just trust my process, just put the work in."

The work has paid off. Coming into fall camp, Offord is competing for a role in the secondary rotation at both field and boundary corner, as well as in the slot. With more reps in Chris Hampton's defense, Offord is settling in and ready to be a steady contributor in several areas this season.

The transition from high school to college football is often overlooked for high-profile recruits like Offord. The talent is obvious, but the process can sometimes take more effort. Dan Lanning has noticed the extra work Offord has put in between seasons, preparing for a sophomore leap into stardom with the Ducks.

"It's night and day. Na'eem is a great example of knowledge of the game," Lanning said. "This guy sees the coverage and the play, and there's still plenty to clean up, but he's proving to be a guy that can play significant snaps as long as he continues to improve because his skill set is so unique. He's long, he has great speed, he challenges the ball, he's physical. All those things are really showing up for him so far in fall camp."

You can't teach athletic ability, and Offord has plenty of it. The Ducks coaching staff can teach the defense, however, but it still comes down to the player to find a process that works for them. Oregon's defense demands plenty of attention, which can be difficult for a college freshman to handle.

Offord has worked to find a balance entering year two in Eugene, and it's paying off early in camp.

"Maturing and time management," Offord said. "Just doing the outside things like putting in the extra work, getting in with the coaches, doing the film, all those types of things. And like I said, maturing because every freshman is different. It ain't gonna be the same for everybody. Sometimes you've got to work your way up."

Hampton has focused on versatility in Oregon's secondary this season, moving players around to fit into different roles. Offord noted that he is "comfortable anywhere" in the defense, which is a big leap from his freshman year in both confidence and understanding of how the unit around him operates.

There is plenty of time remaining in fall camp to nail down roles and rotations, but Offord figures to be a key member of the secondary again this season, and should be flying around on the back end of the defense when the Ducks scrimmage for the first time in the fall on Saturday.

title: Alex Rodriguez: The Dodgers are ‘great’ for baseball
description: While some fans and media believe the Los Angeles Dodgers are ruining Major League Baseball, Alex Rodriguez appears to be a fan of their spending. After admitting he voted in Awful Announcing’s 2026 MLB local TV announcer rankings during an appearance on The Michael Kay Show on ESPN New York, the discussion turned to the…
fullText:
While some fans and media believe the Los Angeles Dodgers are ruining Major League Baseball, Alex Rodriguez appears to be a fan of their spending.

After admitting he voted in Awful Announcing's 2026 MLB local TV announcer rankings during an appearance on The Michael Kay Show on ESPN New York, the discussion turned to the current state of the Yankees, who have been ravaged by injuries and offensive struggles. And while the Yankees remain favorites to win the American League pennant, Kay asked Rodriguez about their biggest potential hurdle to a World Series.

The rich got richer at the trade deadline, when the Dodgers added two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. It reignited conversations about whether the Dodgers are good for baseball or will end up driving owners to continue their push for a hard salary cap during the current labor negotiations. And after Kay held firm that the Dodgers are good for baseball, Rodriguez agreed.

"I think it's great. You and I both would be hypocrites if we said it's not good when we saw what happened in the '90s here in New York, what happened in '09 when Hal Steinbrenner flexed his financial resources to go out and get CC Sabathia, Mark Teixeira and A.J. Burnett and the year before we had Johnny Damon," Rodriguez told Kay.

Rodriguez noted that the key to spending money is not making mistakes, suggesting that the $22 million the Yankees spent on outfielder Trent Grisham may have been a mistake. Similarly, the Dodgers shelled out massive contracts for Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz in the offseason, which have yet to pan out.

As a former player, current broadcaster and franchise owner, albeit in the NBA with the Minnesota Timberwolves, Rodriguez is in a unique position to weigh in on the Dodgers. It's hard for Rodriguez to be against the Dodgers flexing their resources considering he signed a groundbreaking 10-year, $252 million contract with the Texas Rangers in 2000 before playing for the Yankees during their peak spending era. It would also be hard for Rodriguez to rant against a salary cap, given that he's an NBA owner with a soft cap.

If the Dodgers win their third World Series in a row after adding Skubal to a star-studded roster highlighted by Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, and Freddie Freeman, the calls for MLB to fix its financial imbalance will grow as they head toward a lockout. But the Dodgers' ability to play the role of the villain also undoubtedly makes the playoffs more compelling, which is why they're still great for baseball.

The post Alex Rodriguez: The Dodgers are 'great' for baseball appeared first on Awful Announcing.

title: Youri Tielemans reveals why he couldn’t refuse 'step above' Manchester United move
description: Youri Tielemans has explained why he could not turn down a move to Manchester United this summer.Tielemans signed for Manchester United fromAston Villa in a £35m deal earlier this summer, after the R...
fullText:
Youri Tielemans has explained why he could not turn down a move to Manchester United this summer.

Tielemans signed for Manchester United fromAston Villa in a £35m deal earlier this summer, after the Red Devils activated his modest release clause at Villa Park.

The 29-year-old's move came as a surprise, with Manchester United moving quickly to tie up a deal as Michael Carrick reshapes his midfield at Old Trafford.

He made his first appearance for the club as a substitute during the 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain at the weekend.

Tielemans has helped both Leicester City and Aston Villa to major trophies during his time in English football, includingEuropa League success with the latter last season.

The Belgium international admits that success was an 'amazing' experience, but said the opportunity to sign for Manchester United was too good to turn down. He expressed his gratitude to Aston Villa but said a move to Manchester represents a step 'above'.

"I know that at Villa we did amazing things," Tielemans said toSky Sports.

"We achieved the Europa League win which was great for the club but there are still clubs above Aston Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.

"Especially at this moment, there is a very positive mood in and around the club so I am just hopeful that we can have a great story together.

"Aston Villa is a great club and I owe them the world. They have put me back at my best level so I am very thankful."

title: Real Madrid talisman finally returns to training as Mourinho gets full group together

fullText:
Jose Mourinho finally has his full Real Madrid squad back together after Jude Bellingham returned to training following his extended summer break.

The England international completed his commercial commitments in London before making his way back to the club, becoming the final World Cup international to report for duty.

As the clubBellingham took part in the afternoon session alongside the players who were not selected for Real Madrid's Teresa Herrera Trophy meeting with Deportivo La Coruna at Riazor.

The midfielder is also said to be in excellent physical condition, meaning there should be little concern over his fitness as he begins his preparations.

However, Bellingham will not feature against Deportivo.

Bellingham's arrival completes an important stage of Real Madrid's pre-season preparations.

The 23-year-old had been given additional time away following his international commitments, while several of his teammates had already returned to work earlier in the week.

Mourinho now has the majority of his senior group available, although the players who recently reported back are still being managed carefully.

Bellingham trained with and without the ball during the session, beginning the process of getting back up to full match sharpness.

The midfielder was joined by the injured members of the squad, although those players followed individual programmes.

Jude Bellingham is the last player to rejoin training after the World Cup. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Bellingham's first opportunity to play under Mourinho is now expected to come against Schalke on Sunday, August 16.
