Speaking of the Teresa Herrera Trophy, Kylian Mbappe, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate and Aurelien Tchouameni are all unavailable for the trip to Riazor despite having returned to training earlier this week.

Rather than immediately throwing the returning internationals into action, Mourinho is giving them time to build their fitness and adapt to the workload.

title: Rashee Rice: ‘I’ve got the right group of guys around me’
description: On Tuesday, Kansas City’s polarizing wideout discussed an offseason spent in jail and recovering from knee surgery.
fullText:
On Tuesday, fans of the Kansas City Chiefs finally heard from the most controversial player at the team's training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph.

Wide receiver Rashee Rice missed most of the offseason program after a parole violation accelerated a jail sentence. This summer, Rice was ordered to serve 30 days in jail as part of a 2025 plea deal for a 2024 street-racing-related car crash in Dallas.

Originally, Rice was able to serve the jail time at his own discretion during the five-year probation period. After reportedly testing positive for THC, however, the Dallas County court ordered him to report to jail immediately.

Rice was short on words in his description of the month and the lessons learned.

"A learning experience and a reality check," he remarked. "Don't focus on the past. Focus on what's going on now."

His focus has also turned to a more limited group of influences around him and improved mental health.

"I'm doing good mentally," Rice assessed. "I've got the right group of guys around me. Good agents. Good coaches. Small circle on anybody else outside that's not part of the football team. Just keeping my head straight and also keeping me in a positive attitude."

The jail time was not the only limiting factor in Rice's offseason. As we learned of his imminent incarceration, we also learned that the wideout underwent a knee cleanup procedure. Previously, Rice suffered a torn LCL in 2023 that robbed him of much of his second season.

After leaving practice early to work with trainers in the first two weeks of camp, Rice is now participating more fully in team periods.

He did not realize the procedure was needed until late in the spring.

"Honestly, I thought it was probably just a little bit of swelling," Rice explained. "I didn't know it was something that needed to have surgery. We're kind of taught to just keep going until you can't anymore. It was a perfect time for me to get it cleaned up so it wouldn't affect me for the season. I was ready to go, regardless."

As he ramped up his knee rehab following his release, Rice found motivation working alongside quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Mahomes has spent his offseason recovering from a major knee injury suffered in December.

"The best part about it was being there with Pat," Rice revealed. "Knowing that he had a more serious surgery and how hard he was working just kind of motivated me. Then, he's pulling the craziest cars every day, so he's my motivation every morning."

Through three seasons, Rice has teased game-breaking talent while also finding himself unavailable both due to injuries and a league suspension to open the 2025 season. Rice was asked to describe what he brings to a team beneath the surface of troubling headlines.

"I would say I'm a positive guy," he offered. "I'm a great person to feed off of as far as energy. A smiling guy, mostly at all times. Unless it's time for work, [then] I'm serious. Then, I'm a father. I take the most responsibility in being a good father to my boys."

That serious work now finds the wide receiver room under stricter management from the coaching staff. Rice now plays under veteran receivers coach Chad O'Shea and longtime Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, returning to Kansas City after a three-year absence.

When he has been available, Rice has often commanded a disproportionate target share in the passing offense. Under Bieniemy and O'Shea, he has been working on what he can do to help his teammates, even if he knows a called play is not coming to him.

He expects big things from the wide receiver room he shares with Xavier Worthy, Tyquan Thornton and rookie Cyrus Allen.

"We're going to do some amazing things," Rice predicted. "Not only because we're great receivers, but because we've got a good coaching staff around us as well as a great quarterback and a foundation in general."

That foundation has Rice in a good place after a dreadful offseason.

"I'm 100% locked in on what's going on now with the team," Rice declared. "I'm ready to go out there and dominate. I've got a good brotherhood behind me."

title: Cal Raleigh responds to Dan Wilson criticism from the Seattle Mariners fanbase
description: The Seattle Mariners just cannot put together any positive run of form this season after losing yet again on Tuesday. Dan Wilson is coming under heavy criticism up in the Pacific Northwest as the Mariners have slipped to a 56-64 record on the year.
fullText:
The Seattle Mariners just cannot put together any positive run of form this season after losing yet again on Tuesday.

Dan Wilson is coming under heavy criticism up in the Pacific Northwest as the Mariners have slipped to a 56-64 record on the year.

Defeat on Tuesday evening against the New York Yankees was expected, but goes to show the huge regression on display from this time last year.

Cal Raleigh was one of the leaders in the Mariners' team last season dragging them through to the postseason.

However, he has also seen a considerable downfall in his output after scoring a 60 home run season last year.

Having seen the criticism directed towards the manager, Raleigh has shared his thoughts on who deserves the blame in Seattle.

The Mariners look like a shadow of their former selves having pushed the Toronto Blue Jays last season in the Championship Series.

There has not been much to cheer for this season, with Raleigh a prime example of the backward step taken by the team this season.

The catcher admitted he is also to blame as he responded to some of the criticism being received by his manager from the fans in Seattle.

"Ultimately, the players decide the outcome of these games. Obviously, Dan has the say on who comes in and writes the lineup, and we understand that," Raleigh told the media.

"But at the end of the day, those 26 guys have to be ready to play, and we have to rely on each other. That's where the performance comes from.

"Dan's not out there playing. Edgar's [Martinez] not out there playing. Woody's not out there pitching. It comes down to the 26 guys in that locker room, and we're going to have to lean on some different guys each night."

"That starts in the clubhouse. We just have to do a better job of relaying that and understanding that you can't point fingers."

Ultimately, actions speak louder than words and the Mariners are in serious need of some of their star players stepping up at the plate.

Raleigh was high-flying last year and even competing for the MVP award, yet he has scored just one home run this season.

Fingers are being pointed outside the team, but it seems as if the likes of Raleigh are trying to keep things cool in-house.

title: 2028 5-Star WR Brysen Wright locks in game day visit with Florida
description: Five-star wide receiver and No. 1 overall prospect in the 2028 class, Brysen Wright has locked in a fall visit with the Florida Gators.
fullText:
Five-star wide receiver Brysen Wright has scheduled a game-day visit to Florida on Sept. 26, according to Rivals' Chad Simmons. The Jacksonville, Florida, native is heralded as the top recruit in the 2028 class.

Listed at 6-feet-3.5-inches and 215 pounds, Wright already has SEC size. Landing him would be a tremendous victory for the program as new head coach Jon Sumrall aims to keep elite in-state talent at home.

The Gators have been involved with Wright for years, offering him while he was still in the eighth grade, back in 2024. He was in Gainesville this past June for an unofficial visit, and reports surrounding his recruitment imply that the All-First Coast selection is the No. 1 priority for the Gators 2028 cycle.

During his standout sophomore season at Mandarin High School, Wright caught 46 passes for 983 yards and 10 touchdowns. According to MaxPreps, the playmaker eclipsed 1,500 all-purpose yards last year, also showcasing his abilities on special teams.

Wright was named the 2025 NFL Flag Player of the Year after leading the 14U division with 10 touchdowns and going viral for an eye-popping one-hand catch that drew praise from several NFL superstars, including Patrick Mahomes.

The Gators will be up against tough competition as the Longhorns covet Wright as well. He visited Austin in April and will return to Texas on Sept. 12.

Wright is ranked the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2028 class according to 247Sports Composite, a rating that is mirrored by On3's industry rankings. He has 32 total offers, including invitations from 10 other SEC programs; among them are Alabama, Auburn and Georgia.

Rivals recruiting prediction machine suggests that the Gators hold the second-best odds to land the blue-chip recruit at 10.2%, with Miami leading the way at 31.1%.

title: Ja'Kobi Lane is turning heads early at Ravens camp
description: Having been a highlight reel playmaker at USC, Ja'Kobi Lane is carrying that knack for the impressive splash play into the NFL
fullText:
Ja'Kobi Lane at USC was a dynamic weapon with a unique skill set that, at times, made him unguardable. Now in the NFL, that skill set will be used to help one of the best quarterbacks in the league, Lamar Jackson, get back to playing like an MVP.

In a recent article, Jamison Hensley discusses how former Trojan Ja'Kobi Lane is faring at Ravens training camp. Here is what he had to say:

"Later, in one-on-one drills, Lane showed his playmaking ability again, using a double move to get behind cornerback T.J. Tampa and catching a long touchdown pass from Jackson.

This has been an outstanding start to camp for Lane, a third-round pick from USC who has become the team's No. 3 wide receiver behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. On Thursday, Lane first electrified the crowd by elevating over two defenders for a leaping, 30-yard catch over the middle."

Lamar now having a physical threat to get the ball to on the outside will only elevate the Ravens' offense. That is the one thing Jackson has missed so far in his career in Baltimore. Lane is making a name for himself at Ravens camp, but anyone who watched the Trojans last year or the last few seasons knows that is not surprising in the slightest. The Ravens were already an imposing and lethal offense; now, after adding a USC Trojan, they are going to take it to a new level.

title: Dodgers Ace Dominates Royals In Dazzling Return From IL
description: Blake Snell didn't skip a beat
fullText:
The loaded Los Angeles Dodgers got another star back on Tuesday night as Blake Snell returned from the injured list at Dodger Stadium.

Making his first start since May 9 after undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies from his pitching elbow, Snell didn't skip a beat. The two-time Cy Young winner racked up 10 strikeouts over six innings of one-run ball against the Kansas City Royals, allowing just three hits and one walk while throwing 55 of his 84 pitches for strikes.

His gem helped the Dodgers to a 5-4 win and their second straight victory, improving their NL West-leading record to 72-48.

It was only Snell's second start of the season for Los Angeles, as he also missed the first six weeks with an injury. That's been a theme for Snell throughout his career, unfortunately, as the 33-year-old southpaw has often been plagued by injuries and inconsistency.

When he's right, however, he can be one of the most dominant pitchers in baseball. If he can stay healthy down the stretch, he could give the Dodgers a huge boost in October as they seek their third straight championship.

While the Royals were an easy matchup, he'll face a much tougher test in his next scheduled outing against the Milwaukee Brewers at home on Sunday.

title: Iconic indoor event Tennent's Soccer Sixes returns
description: All 12 Scottish Premiership clubs will enter teams into a legends version of cult indoor tournament the Tennent's Soccer Sixes later this year.
fullText:
All 12 Scottish Premiership clubs will enter a team into a legends version of cult indoor tournament the Tennent's Soccer Sixes later this year.

The revived event, backed by the SPFL, will take place at Braehead Arena on the weekend of 3 and 4 October and be broadcast on Premier Sports.

Group stages will be played on Saturday, with the winner and runner-up from three regionalised groups of four teams progressing to the knockout stage along with the two best third-placed teams.

Every game will have a winner, with a bonus point for a penalty shootout win in the event of a draw after normal time. The sin bin will also be in operation.

The Tennent's Soccer Sixes was a staple of the Scottish football scene for nine years from 1984, with clubs fielding many of their leading players.

Partick Thistle, who are in the Scottish Championship and therefore will not play in this year's revived event, were the winners of last tournament in 1993.

SPFL chief executive Neil Doncaster said: "The Tennent's Sixes has a special place in the hearts and minds of a generation of football fans and we are absolutely thrilled to get the band back together again with the official endorsement of the SPFL."

title: Trump's approval rating hits yet another record low in latest poll
description: President Trump’s approval rating has fallen to yet another low for his second term in the White House, according to a new Economist/YouGov poll.
fullText:
President Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to yet another low since his return to the White House, according to a new Economist/YouGov poll, which also found that just 1 in 3 Americans approve of his job performance.

The survey, released Aug. 11, found that 33% of Americans approve of Trump's performance, down 3 percentage points from the previous week. This marks the lowest approval rating the president has seen in YouGov tracking since he returned to office in 2025.

Apart from his continued slump in the polls, a majority of Americans, 60%, said they perceived the president as "not honest and trustworthy". According to the newest poll, 65% of respondents said the country is headed in the wrong direction, up 2 percentage points from the Economist/YouGov's poll in late July.

The latest poll also found that Trump's age continues to concern the American public, with 53% saying they believed the 80-year-old president was too old to be in the White House.

The Economist/YouGov poll was conducted Aug. 7-10 among 1,589 U.S. adults. The poll's margin of error was plus or minus 3.2 percentage points.

Trump's slide in the polls in recent weeks could signify good news for Democrats ahead of November's midterm elections. In the newest Economist/YouGov poll, Democrats hold an 8-point lead over the GOP in a generic congressional ballot.

That lead has held in other surveys, as a poll released by Marquette Law School on Aug. 5 showed Democrats holding a 6-point advantage over Republicans. Another survey released Aug. 3 by Reuters/Ipsos had the Democratic Party holding a 5-point lead over the GOP.

Last week, Trump said the Republican base is angry at the party's leadership in Congress, not him, ahead of the midterms.

"A lot of them are very angry at Republicans, to be honest with you," Trump said in an interview with Punchbowl News. "They're angry at Republicans, but they're not angry at me."

The president's remarks came as he dismissed his current approval ratings by defending his popularity, specifically pointing to his 2024 election wins in several states.

"I have records in many of the states," Trump said. "The question is ... if I don't run, will those people go out and vote? And that's the one thing I can't tell you. I'm going to ask them to."

Aside from Trump's continued struggles with his approval rating, a majority of respondents in the newest poll also said they believed the president is using his presidential powers for his own benefit.

According to the Economist/YouGov poll, 61% of respondents said they believed Trump was using his office for personal gain, and 55% said they believed the president was using the Department of Justice to go after his political enemies.

Trump's controversial East Wing ballroom in the White House has also remained unpopular with Americans, with 57% saying they oppose it.

While individual polls vary, major polling averages continue to show Trump in negative territory overall:

RealClearPolitics (Aug. 11): 39.2% approve, 58.6% disapprove

New York Times (Aug. 11): 37% approve, 59% disapprove

Silver Bulletin (Aug. 11): 38.1% approve, 58.5% disapprove

USA TODAY's Kinsey Crowley contributed to this report.

title: Man City sign goalkeeper Rulli from Marseille
description: Manchester City complete the signing of Argentina goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille.
fullText:
Manchester City have completed the signing of Argentina goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille.

The 34-year-old returns to Etihad Stadium - where he spent the 2016-17 season without making a first-team appearance - on a two-year deal.

BBC Sport previously reported that City have paid a fee of £1.7m.

He comes in as a replacement for England goalkeeper James Trafford, who left City to join Leeds in a deal worth up to £45m, and will be understudy to number one Gianluigi Donnarumma.

"This is an amazing opportunity for me and one I had to grasp. When the chance to join Manchester City comes along you have to go for it," Rulli said.

"Everyone knows what an impressive club this is. City's success over a long time has been impressive. Everyone I have spoken to about City said I had to join them because they are a club with incredibly high standards.

"Every professional wants to be in a high-performance environment and I can't wait to get started because I know I will improve and learn, which is always my main priority."

Rulli famously scored a penalty in Villarreal's 2021 Europa League final victory over Manchester United, before denying opposite number David de Gea to decide the marathon shootout.

He has won eight caps for Argentina and was part of the squad that won the 2022 World Cup and 2024 Copa America, and reached the 2026 World Cup final.

Rulli has also had spells at clubs around Europe including Real Sociedad, Montpellier and Ajax.

title: Why 'wanted' Stanway wasted no time in getting Arsenal tattoo
description: England midfielder Georgia Stanway explains her latest tattoo and how Arsenal made her "feel wanted" before her move from Bayern Munich.
fullText:
Georgia Stanway's move to Arsenal has already had an impact on her body - in the form of yet another tattoo for the England midfielder.

Last month when she joined from Bayern Munich, Stanway's signing reveal video showed her having the words 'Whatever the weather' inked on to her right arm - lyrics from the club anthem North London Forever.

Decorating her skin is nothing new to the 27-year-old, who estimates she has close to 200 tattoos, external and has developed her skills as an artist in her own right.

Her clients include England team-mate Beth Mead, longtime servant of Arsenal and now of Manchester City - but Stanway is certainly not calling time on customising her own body.

"You see the tattoos - I see the skin," she said. "So much more to come!"

Arsenal sign Lioness Stanway from Bayern

Watch: Lioness Stanway tattoos someone for the first time. Video, 00:05:30

Stanway's arrival at Arsenal on a free transfer from Bayern is one of the most high-profile moves of an eye-catching transfer window in the Women's Super League (WSL).

The midfielder enjoyed four trophy-laden years with the German club, and boasts two European Championship winners' medals with England.

A long-established totem in Sarina Wiegman's Lionesses side, Stanway told the Women's Football Weekly podcast how playing in the Bundesliga has developed her game.

"I've massively changed as a player and as a person," she said. "I've got more comfortable with myself and I enjoy my own time a lot more.

"Munich also gave me the opportunity to develop a position and to figure out how I wanted to play with trust and expectation from the manager."

She arrives at Emirates Stadium in her prime and ready to ignite Arsenal's push for a first WSL title since 2018-19.

She explains that once aware of their interest, there was only one club in the running for her signature.

"I knew I wanted to take the next step," she said. "I really like the fact Arsenal came in for me when I wasn't available. It's a really nice feeling to be wanted.

"What Arsenal are building within England, within the WSL, within Europe, is something I want to be part of.

"It's setting the standard with women's football."

Last season, Arsenal finished second to Stanway's former club Manchester City but have made changes this summer, with Mead among those to leave and seven new signings through the door.

Among them are Barcelona and Spain full-back Ona Batlle, Switzerland midfielder Geraldine Reuteler and exciting young forward Lisa Baum, with the latter two also arriving from German football.

"It's a little bit of a new chapter," Stanway said. "A lot of quality has come in. Arsenal obviously went hunting in the Bundesliga, which is a league that sometimes goes under the radar.

"From the outside, everybody wants to be a part of Arsenal and what they're about to create."

While excited about her football ambitions, Stanway does concede that living in London is a new challenge.

Having grown up in the Cumbrian town of Barrow-in-Furness, she conceded that being around the capital city "will take a little bit of adjusting".

"I'm a bit of a homebody and I'm so used to everything being so local," she said. "I've already said to the girls about places being so far away and they're like, 'It's only an hour'.

"I like little things within the countryside, I like farms, so I don't think I'll be in the city too much!"

title: This Missouri school named the best community college in the nation
description: See why WalletHub ranked this Missouri community college as the best in the nation.
fullText:
Community colleges can offer students a quality education and access to career opportunities post-graduation, at a fraction of the cost of many four-year institutions.

For instance, during the 2025-26 school year, tuition for a full-time undergraduate program at a public four-year university was nearly three times higher on average than tuition at a public two-year in-district community college, according to College Board.

For those considering the community college route, you'll find one of the best in Missouri.

WalletHub, the personal finance company released a study examining the best and worst community colleges in the country for 2026.

WalletHub ranked State Technical College of Missouri No. 1 in its community colleges ranking.

In its analysis, WalletHub compared more than 610 community colleges across 18 key indicators, including cost of in-state tuition and graduation rate. Those metrics were then grouped into three categories — Cost & Financing, Education Outcomes and Career Outcomes — to determine each state's overall score.

State Tech ranked among the top five nationally for both education outcomes and career outcomes, which isn't too surprising given the school bills itself as "The Employers' Choice." Its score in cost & financing, meanwhile, was more middle-of-the-road.

State Tech earned a total score of 73.99 out of 100.

"The State Technical College of Missouri, located in Osage County, MO, is the best community college, in part because 90% of students stay with the school from the first year to the second year, the best retention rate in the country, and 79% of students graduate – the best graduation rate in the country.

In addition, the school's students receive the third-largest amount of grant or scholarship aid, at an average of $9,223 per student. This helps make it extremely unlikely that students will default on any loans they do have to take out.

Lastly, the State Technical College of Missouri also offers credit for life experiences and provides employment services to students, which can help them graduate more quickly and obtain jobs sooner."

Several other Missouri community colleges also made the list, but none came anywhere near State Tech's ranking.

title: Kick It Out chair Bhandari to step down from role
description: Kick It Out chair Sanjay Bhandari will step down from his role at the end of the 2026-27 season.
fullText:
Kick It Out chair Sanjay Bhandari will step down from his role at the end of the 2026-27 season.

Bhandari was appointed chair in 2019 and will leave after more than seven years in the position.

He was awarded an MBE in 2024 for his services to football during his time with the charity, which was established in 1993.

In a statement, Bhandari said it has been a "tremendous honour" to chair Kick It Out.

"Our 'Football United' strategy is deliberately built on a vision of bringing together governing bodies, clubs, players, supporters, communities and partners to create lasting change.

"In a world that often feels increasingly negative and divided, we are consciously seeking to strike a different tone.

"The new chair will play a pivotal role in helping Kick It Out deliver that vision, by leading an experienced and committed board, and working closely with our chief executive to represent an organisation that has become one of the most respected voices for equality and inclusion in sport."

During his tenure, Bhandari oversaw a transformation of the organisation. This included improved financial independence and governance, the appointment of an entirely new board and leadership team, and a new team structure.

Kick It Out will now begin a recruitment process to identify a preferred candidate by the end of December.

The new chair is expected to work alongside Bhandari until the end of the 2026-27 campaign before formally taking charge on 1 July 2027.

title: Sport events in the UK affected by eclipse
description: The horse racing meeting at Ffos Las in South Wales will begin about two hours earlier on Wednesday because of the solar eclipse.
fullText:
The horse racing meeting at Ffos Las in South Wales will begin about two hours earlier on Wednesday because of the solar eclipse.

The UK and parts of Europe are set to experience the most significant solar eclipse in nearly three decades, which is set to begin shortly after 18:00 BST.

At other sporting events, including four Hundred cricket matches on Wednesday, floodlights will be turned on throughout matches.

It will be the most dramatic eclipse visible from the UK since 1999, and the first time a total eclipse can be seen from continental Europe since then too.

At Ffos Las, the first race was scheduled for 17:40 BST but that has now been rescheduled by the British Horseracing Authority to 15:35.

Officials at Kempton racecourse, which has races scheduled for 19:00 and 19:30, said there will be no disruption as all races were set to be under floodlights.

During the solar eclipse in August 1999, a League Cup football match between Torquay United and Portsmouth at Plainmoor stadium was postponed.

Devon and Cornwall Police forced the delay because an influx of tourists travelling to the English coast left local authorities under-staffed to safely manage stadium crowds.

title: Torres misses Barcelona training to finalise PSG move
description: Spain's World Cup hero Ferran Torres is given permission to miss Barcelona training to finalise a move to Paris St-Germain.
fullText:
Spain's World Cup hero Ferran Torres has been given permission to miss Barcelona training to finalise a move to Paris St-Germain.

Torres, 26, scored an extra-time winner against Argentina to help Spain claim their second World Cup this summer.

He had been due to return to training with the Catalan giants on Wednesday but will not do so as a move to PSG gets closer.

The deal with PSG, who play in the Super Cup final against Aston Villa on Wednesday night in Salzburg, is likely to be worth more than £40m.

Torres only has one year left on his contract at Barcelona and some fans have been frustrated that the forward has spoken openly about the possibility of leaving the club.

Speaking on a media tour of the United States following Spain's World Cup win, he said: "I have a contract with Barcelona but, in football, you never know."

Asked directly about links with PSG, he added: "Every time these teams want you it's a good thing.

"You never know because in football everything can change in one minute, so I have to be ready for everything."

PSG have won the Champions League in the past two seasons and are managed by former Barcelona coach and player Luis Enrique.

The Parisians could lose Bradley Barcola this summer, with the forward wanted by Liverpool.

Torres has been at Barcelona since 2022 having previously spent two years at Manchester City. He has scored 25 goals in 65 appearances for Spain.

title: Putin threatens retaliation for Western seizures of Russian commercial vessels
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened retaliation for Western seizures of its commercial vessels, describing them as “piracy.”  Speaking on a visit to a Russian warship that was tak...
fullText:
MOSCOW (AP) — Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened retaliation for Western seizures of its commercial vessels, describing them as "piracy."

Speaking on a visit to a Russian warship that was taking part in a naval exercise in the Pacific, Putin described the Western moves to detain vessels linked to Russia as a breach of international maritime law.

"It's nothing but piracy and robbery," Putin said. "If this is done, we will be forced to respond in kind."

He added that the Russian response wouldn't necessarily come in the waters where the Russian ships were seized, noting that Moscow could retaliate "in any area where we see it as necessary and appropriate," including in the Pacific.

The Pacific Fleet chief, Adm. Viktor Liina, reported to Putin that the navy was ready to start inspections of the commercial ships serving the "unfriendly nations." He noted that many of the ships operated by British, French and other European carriers fly the flags of other nations, effectively making them a "shadow fleet."

"We have enough assets for inspection and detention of vessels of the unfriendly nations and their shadow fleet," Liina told Putin. "We are ready to start performing the task."

Russia is believed to be using a fleet of hundreds of ships to evade international sanctions imposed after Moscow sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022.

France and the U.K. have detained tankers suspected of being of Russia's "shadow fleet" shipping oil in violation of international sanctions. The EU has sanctioned hundreds of "shadow fleet" ships.

Russia has recently started deploying warships to escort its commercial vessels.

Dmitry Medvedev, who served as Russia's president in 2008-2012 to let Putin observe term limits and is now deputy head of Russia's Security Council, noted that many ships belonging to European carriers fly the so-called "flags of convenience" just like Russian carriers do.

"It means that by applying a symmetrical approach, which is only fair, Russia has the right to attack any merchant vessel belonging to hostile nations, whether in our waters or in neutral waters, provided there are reasonable grounds to suspect it is carrying cargo in the enemy's interest, and that applies to any cargo," Medvedev said. "There are a great many such vessels, and our military is capable of dramatically expanding operations well beyond the Black Sea basin."

title: Palestinian students and staff sue Columbia University alleging discrimination
description: A group of current and former Palestinian students and staff have sued Columbia University, alleging discriminatory treatment by the school against its
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Aug 11 (Reuters) - A group of current and former Palestinian students and staff have sued Columbia University, alleging ‌discriminatory treatment by the school against its Palestinian community since ‌late 2023, according to a court filing in New York.

• The lawsuit said the university ​failed to protect its Palestinian members from harassment and targeted them through what it cast as "unfair and biased disciplinary hearings."

• Columbia has previously denied being discriminatory and has condemned hate. Local media reported that it declined to comment ‌on pending litigation. It did ⁠not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

• Protests took place at Columbia and around the U.S. after the ⁠start of Israel's assault on Gaza following a deadly Palestinian Hamas attack in October 2023.

• Protesters demanded an end to U.S. support for its ally ​and called ​for the divestment of funds by ​universities from companies supporting Israel.

• ‌In May 2025, Columbia suspended more than 65 students for their role in shutting down the university's main library in a pro-Palestinian demonstration.

• That demonstration came as the university was negotiating with President Donald Trump's administration, which had cut its federal funding after accusing the university of tolerating antisemitism ‌during pro-Palestinian protests.

• Protesters, including some Jewish ​groups, say opposing Israel's assault on Gaza ​and its occupation of Palestinian ​territories is not antisemitic and advocacy for Palestinian rights ‌should not be conflated with supporting extremism.

• ​Columbia agreed to ​pay over $200 million to the U.S. government to resolve federal probes and restore most of the federal funding in July last year.

• ​Free speech groups condemned ‌Columbia's protest crackdown in which students faced arrests, suspensions, expulsions and ​degree revocations.

title: A Gun Ruling Highlights the Tricks Congress Uses To Evade Limits on Its Power
description: During the last century, the Commerce Clause has replaced the Taxing Clause as an excuse for federal legislation.
fullText:
Second Amendment groups applauded last week after a federal judge in Texas ruled that several national firearm regulations were unconstitutional. But the decision did not hinge on gun rights. Rather, it affirmed a broader principle: The federal government's powers are limited to those explicitly granted by the Constitution.

The case involved the National Firearms Act (NFA), a 1934 law that targeted weapons and accessories thought to be favored by criminals. Because that law was framed as a revenue measure, U.S. District Judge James Hendrix held, Congress fatally undermined the constitutional rationale for some of its provisions by eliminating the federal taxes on making and transferring sound suppressors, short-barreled rifles, and short-barreled shotguns.

Congress did that last year, when it approved a law that retained the NFA's taxes on machine guns and "destructive devices" such as bombs and grenades but repealed the taxes on all other products covered by the law. Given that change, Hendrix concluded, the reporting, registration, and record-keeping requirements for the latter set of products, which ostensibly were aimed at facilitating revenue collection, could no longer be justified by the tax power that Congress invoked when it passed the law 92 years ago.

That rationale for the NFA, which was enacted as part of the Internal Revenue Code, may seem puzzling, since Congress has long relied on its power to regulate interstate commerce as an all-purpose license to legislate. But in 1934, legislators did not think that power was broad enough to authorize outright bans on politically disfavored products, an idea that would not gain currency until after the Supreme Court began stretching the Commerce Clause beyond recognition.

Instead of banning the listed weapons, Congress imposed a $200 tax on their production and transfer. That tax, which is equivalent to about $5,000 today, was meant to be prohibitive.

Attorney General Homer Cummings explained the need for that roundabout approach when he testified in favor of the NFA. Although Congress "of course" had "no inherent police powers to go into certain localities and deal with local crime," he said, it could still use "the power of taxation" to restrict weapons it viewed as especially dangerous.

"If we made a statute absolutely forbidding any human being to have a machine gun," Cummings explained, "you might say there is some constitutional question involved. But when you say, 'We will tax the machine gun,' and when you say that the absence of a license showing payment of the tax has been made indicates that a crime has been perpetrated, you are easily within the law."

Congress had taken a similar approach when it approved the Harrison Narcotics Tax Act of 1914, which effectively prohibited nonmedical use of opiates and cocaine. It would likewise rely on "the power of taxation" to justify a de facto national ban on cannabis in 1937.

The Supreme Court blessed that pretext in 1928, upholding the Harrison Act on the grounds that it raised "substantial revenue," consistent with its advertised purpose. But as Hendrix noted, Congress broke that thin reed when it eliminated the taxes on most NFA-regulated products.

The Trump administration argued that the NFA regulations could still be justified under the Commerce Clause. Hendrix, a Trump appointee, disagreed, saying the government "cannot employ post-hoc justifications to save a statute based on an enumerated power that Congress never invoked."

Nowadays, of course, Congress relies on the Commerce Clause to enact all sorts of regulations that were once viewed as beyond its scope, including laws criminalizing conduct that is neither interstate nor commercial. "If Congress can regulate this under the Commerce Clause," Justice Clarence Thomas warned in a 2005 case involving medical marijuana grown and consumed in California, "then it can regulate virtually anything—and the Federal Government is no longer one of limited and enumerated powers."

Hendrix's decision is a welcome reminder of that fundamental principle. But since 1934, Congress has found a new excuse to justify almost anything it wants to do.

The post A Gun Ruling Highlights the Tricks Congress Uses To Evade Limits on Its Power appeared first on Reason.com.

title: England gearing up for WXV with new smaller balls
description: England's Red Roses are in pre-season training before the upcoming WXV Global Series and have been using the controversial smaller balls.
fullText:
England's women are in Nottingham for pre-season this month before the upcoming WXV Global Series.

In the new competition, the Red Roses will take on Australia, Canada and New Zealand on home soil in September before further tests across the Atlantic against Canada again and the USA in October.

The last time we saw the world champions in action they were winning another Six Nations' Grand Slam - so what's new?

Head coach John Mitchell spills the beans.

World Rugby's new size 4.5 balls - about 3% smaller but the same weight as a regulation size five - will be used for the WXV Global Series and are now in use in the England camp.

Their introduction has not been without controversy. In May, England fly-half Zoe Harrison said it is "the worst decision someone has ever made".

Mitchell said the attacking players and kickers were all given one to take home for the holidays but he believes "coaching" was key to the success of teams using it.

"If you want to get better at something, regardless of the size of the ball, it's all about coaching. So I think our girls have been well-coached," he said.

"I think it's too early for for me to say that it's going to help our offloading game or it's going to help out with the pass. I'm sure there's consequences as well.

"There might be more contestable kicking, which is probably something that we want to keep away from our game because it's a point of difference between our game and the men's game."

World Rugby held a trial for the smaller balls with female players on the top-tier Sevens circuit in November.

Mitchell said the trial "certainly might help other teams" but he added conclusions would likely be drawn after the first three Tests at home.

During the summer break, Mitchell officially became a UK citizen, external - something he says he should have done "20 years earlier".

Born and raised in New Zealand, the 62-year-old coached the All Blacks to the semi-finals of the 2003 Rugby World Cup but spent much of his early coaching career in England with Sale Sharks, Wasps and as England men's forwards coach.

The citizenship test involves questions about British history and geography as well as singing the national anthem.

Mitchell said his examiner was struggling to find the national anthem music for him so he happily helped her out, explaining: "'I've got it on my Apple Music, is it OK if I play it?' So I played it and I belted it out, and she goes, 'No-one's ever done that before'.

"I said, 'I've had plenty of practice'."

Last month, Gloucester-Hartpury wing Mia Venner and Exeter scrum-half Flo Robinson were awarded full-time England contracts for the first time, among 32 deals for the 2026-27 season.

When asked about Venner and Robinson's contracts, Mitchell said scrum-half Robinson could be an important part of England's plans.

"Will we get Mo [Natasha Hunt] to the next World Cup? We don't know. So it's very important to make sure that we're growing our next player and Flo's definitely taking that on," he said.

Both Gloucester-Hartpury's Hunt, at age 37, and Harlequins' Marlie Packer, 36, are double world champions and included on the Red Roses' latest contract round.

But with Packer admitting she had considered retirement last season, Mitchell explained that for either player to move on, "somebody's got to come and get their jersey" first.

In the off-season it was confirmed Emily Scarratt had joined the Red Roses set-up full-time as attack and backs coach.

Having taken the role on an interim basis during the Six Nations, Mitchell said that the coaching group is "smarter" with Scarratt's inclusion.

However, the new contract appears to come with more responsibility for the former world player of the year.

Mitchell worked with Scarratt on the attack last season but that will start to evolve. He said: "When Em first started, I didn't want to overwhelm her with a with a whole lot of stuff so I gave her a pretty tight remit.

"You just give away a little bit... She certainly has the ability to take the total attack."

The new WXV Global Series doesn't have a table or a trophy attached to it - it is just Test matches.

"There's no tournament to win so we can be very patient about how we go about things," said Mitchell.

Among the six England games are three against Canada. Having beaten them in the 2025 Rugby World Cup final, it is difficult not to see the fixtures as anything other than a three-Test series and Mitchell thinks the prospect is "really cool".

But with England travelling from Manchester to Exeter, to Twickenham, to Canada and the USA, the schedule is a test of its own.

"It's kind of like you're auditioning for Australia 2029 because geographically we're definitely going to be travelling some distance in this tournament," he said.

"So, I think we're trying to mirror that, understand how important our connections are and play exciting rugby."

title: Fact check: How Tim Scott and a Republican attack ad misleadingly snipped key context from El-Sayed’s ‘dangerous’ speech
description: The leader of Senate Republicans’ campaign arm, Sen. Tim Scott, said in a Sunday interview on CNN that people should believe something Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed supposedly said about ...
fullText:
The leader of Senate Republicans' campaign arm, Sen. Tim Scott, said in a Sunday interview on CNN that people should believe something Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed supposedly said about himself. But Scott took El-Sayed's quote out of context. So did an attack ad released last week by the group Scott chairs.

The National Republican Senatorial Committee's online ad has generated attention and criticism for using the full legal name of El-Sayed, a Muslim former public health official who is running in Michigan against Republican former congressman Mike Rogers. But the ad is also notable for how, like Scott, it uses a misleadingly snipped "dangerous" comment to bolster its case that El-Sayed is a radical.

In the CNN interview on Sunday, Scott claimed of El-Sayed: "He says he's the most dangerous candidate you can find. He's right. We should trust his words, not ours." The 30-second ad features a one-second video clip of El-Sayed shouting, "I'm pretty damn dangerous" – immediately before turning to an attack on El-Sayed's stance toward the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt in the early 2010s.

The full video of El-Sayed's remarks, at a July 25 campaign event during the Democratic primary he won, shows he was arguing that he is an ally to struggling Americans and merely "dangerous" to a list of corporate and political interests he claimed are "rigging our policies against us." The NRSC ad and Scott's remark on CNN didn't acknowledge that the "dangerous" identifier was directed at specific targets, nor that El-Sayed was rejecting the notion that he is broadly "dangerous" to Americans.

El-Sayed said his critics "always use this word around me: dangerous," then added sarcastically, to some audience laughter, "I always wonder, like, why would you call someone like me dangerous? It's not like people who look like me have ever been called dangerous. It's not like you're falling into a well-worn groove that's been around for 25 years calling people who look like me with names like mine dangerous. I know that's not what you're doing, right?"

He continued: "I'll just say this. Go ask a child who needed a pair of glasses in Detroit if I'm dangerous. Go ask the folks who could not breathe because of smokestacks spewing out sulfur dioxide if I'm dangerous. Go ask the parents of kids who are going to schools that were leaded if I'm dangerous. Go ask the people flooded in medical debt if I'm dangerous. I think what they'll tell you is: He's the best friend you might have if you want government to work for you. I'll tell you what: If you're AIPAC, I'm pretty damn dangerous. If you're Big Pharma, I'm dangerous. If you're Big Tech and want to put a data center in your backyard, I'm dangerous. If you're a big bank that wants to collude against us, I am dangerous. If you're a monopolist who wants to raise our prices, I'm dangerous. If you're Chuck Schumer, I'm pretty damn dangerous. And I think it's about damn time we had Democrats who are willing to be dangerous for all the people rigging our policies against us."

In a social media post on the day of El-Sayed's speech, the Republican National Committee posted a 15-second clip of El-Sayed saying: "If you're a big bank that wants to collude against us, I am dangerous. If you're a monopolist who wants to raise our prices, I'm dangerous. If you're Chuck Schumer, I'm pretty damn dangerous."

That's not El-Sayed's entire monologue, of course, but it's a fair edit – clearly demonstrating that El-Sayed was not generally admitting he's a "dangerous" man but rather identifying himself as "dangerous" to big businesses supposedly hurting the public and to Schumer, the Democratic Senate leader the party's left has long criticized.

The NRSC, meanwhile, posted a clip that day showing El-Sayed saying: "If you're Chuck Schumer, I'm pretty damn dangerous." Even that four-second clip was fairer than the one-second, zero-context version of the "dangerous" quote the NRSC used in the ad.

Asked by CNN this week whether the ad did not take El-Sayed's "dangerous" comment significantly out of context, NRSC spokesperson Joanna Rodriguez said in an email, "As you mentioned, yes, Abdul El-Sayed did in fact say he was dangerous." Rodriguez went on to list some El-Sayed remarks she argued were examples of dangerous campaign rhetoric from him and to repeat the attacks from the 30-second ad.

Republicans are entitled to argue that El-Sayed is dangerous and has said dangerous things. But Scott purported to be quoting El-Sayed's own words, and he didn't fairly convey those words. The ad didn't either.

title: Nonu, 44, performs solo haka in response to All Blacks
description: Former All Blacks star Ma'a Nonu responds to the haka by performing one of his own before his side, the Sharks, take on New Zealand in Durban.
fullText:
New Zealand great Ma'a Nonu performed a solo haka in response to the All Blacks' haka before his Sharks side fell to a heavy defeat in Durban.

The All Blacks continued their tour of South Africa with a resounding 54-0 victory, though what happened pre-match will go down in rugby union folklore.

After New Zealand performed their usual Ka Mate haka, Nonu stepped in front of his Sharks team-mates and responded with Kapa o Pango, the All Blacks' alternative haka.

The 44-year-old played 104 matches for New Zealand between 2003 and 2015, and was part of the side that won the Rugby World Cup in 2011 and 2015.

He joined Durban-based Sharks earlier this month to help develop their young players, but a series of injuries and Springbok call-ups saw him called up to the bench.

"On behalf of myself and my family, I thought it was the right thing to do, to answer the boys and the All Blacks," Nonu told SuperSport TV.

"It was such a privilege and an honour, and to do the haka, showing my respect on behalf of my family to the team I love.

"I got nearly 20 minutes off the bench. I tried my best. It was great to see the New Zealand boys."

Nonu, who in 2016 was appointed a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit for services to rugby, spoke to the All Blacks before deciding to perform the solo haka.

"We knew the Ma'a haka was coming," said All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie.

"Ma'a came and saw our defence coach Tana Umaga last night and said he wanted to be respectful and queried about the right way to respond to the haka."

Sharks head coach JP Pietersen praised the impact Nonu has had off the field since joining the team and revealed the veteran was "nervous" about doing a haka alone.

Nonu came off the bench with a quarter to go and landed a big hit on fly-half Ruben Love, who was two years old when Nonu made his New Zealand debut in 2003.

title: How will relegated trio fare in the Championship?
description: BBC Sport England looks at how the three relegated sides - West Ham, Burnley and Wolves - will navigate the Championship this season.
fullText:
With their generous parachute payments, it is often expected those who drop out of the Premier League will be the big contenders to shoot straight back up - but that was not the case last season.

Only Ipswich Town returned to the top flight, and while Southampton did make up for a terrible start under boss Will Still, his replacement Tonda Eckert's spying tactics put an end to their hopes of bouncing back.

And then there was Leicester City, who ultimately failed to escape a double relegation just a decade on from lifting the Premier League trophy.

Yes, the Championship is trickier than some might think. Will the three relegated sides - West Ham United, Burnley and Wolverhampton Wanderers - be able to navigate it?

It has been a whopping 14 years since West Ham have been in the second tier but the side have been in steady decline since the high of winning the Europa Conference League in 2023.

In the end, it came down to a close, fascinating scrap between them and fellow top-flight stalwarts Tottenham Hotspur for survival - but four losses in their final five games sealed the Hammers' fate.

Most of the headlines surrounding West Ham this summer had nothing to do with football.

There was a joint BBC Panorama and The Times investigation into allegations of sexual misconduct against West Ham co-owner David Sullivan, which he categorically denies.

This was followed by Vanessa Gold, West Ham's co-chair, confirming her family's plans to sell its shares in the club to a consortium headed by ex-Newcastle United co-owner Amanda Staveley.

However, fellow co-chair Daniel Kretinsky sold just over 2% of his stake in the club to Czech businessman Jakub Havrlant, making it possible for Kretinsky to purchase Gold's shares under the club's pre-emption rights clause, which gives existing shareholders first refusal on available shares.

The whole process around the sale of Gold's shares could take two months, well into the new season.

What will be key to their success?

The retention of captain Jarrod Bowen is a major bonus for the Hammers.

The 29-year-old forward's skillset should prove tricky for most second-tier defenders. He has also got pace and a high work-rate, which should serve him well in a physical league.

Boss Nuno Espirito Santo could also be influential in West Ham's success.

Despite suffering a poor end to last season, notably he is now the only head coach of the relegated trio to have managerial experience in the English Football League.

The Portuguese took charge of Wolves in 2017 and led them to the Championship title in his first season, and his exploits in the Premier League since, particularly at Molineux and Nottingham Forest, will mean there will be plenty of expectation that he can get them promoted the first time of asking.

Not to forget the power of the fans. London Stadium will be the biggest home ground the Championship has ever seen, housing 62,500 people. That is 51,831 more than Lincoln City's Sincil Bank.

What is the expectation this season?

West Ham are the bookmakers' favourites to win the title and their pedigree alone is enough for their fans to have faith in an immediate bounce back.

Off the field though, the headlines surrounding the club have been a cause of concern and it is not unreasonable to believe the uncertainty could take a toll on the players and coaching staff.

The Hammers did impress with a 3-1 victory over Portsmouth in the first round of the EFL Cup though and their opening game against Burnley on Sunday, 16 August (16:00 BST) could be telling as to how their season will unfold. Dazzle again there and their fans will be blowing their bubbles freely.

Burnley have been on the promotion-swiftly-followed-by-relegation rollercoaster for a few seasons now.

They have experienced four promotions to the Premier League under three different managers since 2014 - Sean Dyche, Vincent Kompany and Scott Parker - and three of those promotions, including their past two, ended in an immediate drop back to the second tier.

Last season's Premier League campaign proved to be their toughest season yet, ending with a mere four wins - just 22 points - to their name.

Burnley's former boss Scott Parker left by mutual consent back in April and the timing of appointing his replacement has left many fans concerned.

Wales head coach Craig Bellamy had been heavily linked with the role in June, with the Clarets approaching the Football Association of Wales in a bid to bring the 47-year-old to Turf Moor.

However, it was not to be. Compensation was seemingly no issue but negotiations for Bellamy's backroom staff to join him at Turf Moor were thought to be a point of contention.

In stepped Genk boss Nicky Hayen, an appointment that had some wondering if it was made out of hope rather than meticulous planning.

What will be key to their success?

Recruitment. The Clarets have seen 12 departures so far this summer and will need to rebuild their squad with a team that fits Hayen's style of play.

The Belgian likes to play high-possession football and wants to be direct once in a position to attack, so players who are good on the ball and able to intercept will be high on his wishlist.

New signing Ugo Raghouber fits that profile perfectly - he's a defensive midfielder who is known for breaking up attacks and he's good in the air.

The only other outfield player the Clarets have purchased this summer, forward Lluc Castell, fits the club's preference for the stars of tomorrow since ALK Capital completed their takeover in 2020.

Of the 20 new players they brought to the club ahead of their promotion-winning Championship campaign in 2024-25, 12 were aged 25 or under.

The following season in the Premier League, the Clarets stuck to this model, with seven of their 15 arrivals being 25 or under. Three were over 30, including veteran defender and former England international Kyle Walker.

Castell shows plenty of promise but, at just 19, is still very much in development.

While a younger squad may have struggled to compete at the top level, it's been effective in the second tier - and Walker will be wanting to add a Championship trophy to the overflowing cabinet filled with accolades from his years at Manchester City.

Burnley know how to run a promotion campaign.

They do not tend to linger in the second tier too long and both previous managers that were appointed by owner Alan Pace - Kompany and Parker - won promotion back to the top flight at the first time of asking.

But yo-yoing between the first and second tiers suggests they have an unsustainable model - and this year could be their most perilous yet.

Walker targets instant Burnley top-flight return

Wolves sunk to the bottom of the Premier League under former boss Vitor Pereira after going winless in their opening 10 games of last season.

Things did seem to take a short upswing when Rob Edwards took the reins in November and they finally got their first victory against West Ham in January, but there would be no miracle escape as they finished 20th in the table and 21 points from safety.

The Wolves fans make no secret of their misgivings over the transfer habits of their club.

Whether it was winger Pedro Neto's departure to Chelsea or Manchester United's swoop for forward Matheus Cunha, for years now Wolves have sold their best players for big money and the weakness of their squad during the 2025-26 season suggested it had not been wisely invested back into the team.

Owners Fosun seemed to have turned a corner, though, in this transfer window, bringing in the experience of full-back Kieran Trippier and keeping hold of midfielder Andre, as well as welcoming back the popular figure of striker Raul Jimenez.

However, the goodwill over Jimenez's return quickly faded with the sacking of Edwards days later and his replacement with little-known Portuguese head coach Cesar Peixoto, external.

That change also seemed to stall Wolves' ambitious start to the transfer window.

What will be key to their success?

Peixoto is known in Portugal for his attacking football and how that transfers into the Championship could be key to how well Wolves perform this season.

The 46-year-old is looking to stamp his aggressive but pragmatic identity on to his new side.

A high press could feature often in Wolves' upcoming campaign but he will also be looking for cool heads and smart football.

All of this is just theory though as Peixoto is untested in English football and he has inherited a side that struggled to keep it together under the pressure of the Premier League.

The appointment feels risky - even more so given many fans felt Edwards' arrival last season was intended for life back in the Championship after he took Luton Town to the top flight in 2023.

Trippier and Jimenez, both 35, joined with Edwards in the managerial seat, bringing the much-needed experience Wolves required.

The talent of 18-year-old Mateus Mane was one of the few highlights in a poor Premier League season and undoubtedly fans will be hoping to see more exciting fresh faces signed before the summer transfer window closes.

What is the expectation this season?

Wolves will be hoping lightning strikes twice and that, as with their memorable 2017-18 title-winning season, a mysterious, untested Portuguese manager will lead them to glory.

He may have a lack of experience in English football but there is plenty of it in the dressing room thanks to the new signings and Peixoto's attacking football could inject a little life into a disillusioned Molineux.

The relationship between the fans and Fosun remains frosty though and you have to feel only a strong season will help to repair the damage done over several years of disappointing transfer windows.

It's a new era, the past is the past - Peixoto

You can catch all the action from the opening weekend of the Championship right here on the BBC Sport website with live text coverage across all three days, starting with Wolves v Blackburn Rovers on Friday at 20:00 BST.

title: The late-bloomer left-back joining Chelsea for £16m
description: Pep Chavarria joins Chelsea on a five-year deal, having played in the Spanish lower leagues until he was 24.
fullText:
Pep Chavarria's path to Stamford Bridge has been anything but conventional.

Unlike many players who reach elite clubs through prestigious academies or early top-flight breakthroughs, Chavarria had to take the longer route.

He did not make his La Liga debut until the age of 24, an age when many players have already established themselves at the highest level.

After spending four years at Rayo Vallecano, the left-back has completed the biggest move of his career, joining Chelsea in a five-year deal worth about £16.3m plus a further £1.7m in add-ons.

"I'm so excited to get started," the 28-year-old said.

"This is a dream for me as Chelsea are one of the biggest clubs in the world. It is a big opportunity but I am prepared and will work hard to help the team achieve success."

BBC Sport looks at how Chavarria went from Spain's lower leagues to earning a move to one of Europe's elite clubs.

Born in Figueres, a city in Catalonia in north-eastern Spain, Chavarria played for his hometown club before moving to Olot, where he built his reputation in Spain's lower tiers.

A move to Real Zaragoza in 2020 gave him his first taste of professional football at a bigger club, and - after two seasons in Spain's second division - he earned the opportunity to step into La Liga with Rayo Vallecano in 2022.

That timing was significant. Rayo were not expected to compete with Spain's established giants, but under a strong collective structure they became one of the division's most difficult opponents.

Rayo's ability to compete against wealthier clubs has repeatedly relied on identifying undervalued players and maximising their strengths, and Chavarria became another example of that model - joining for less than £2m.

At Vallecas, Chavarria developed into a dependable top-flight full-back, combining defensive aggression with the physicality required to succeed in the role.

He made 125 appearances for Rayo and became a regular presence on the left side of defence.

Joining Rayo also gave him the chance to play in front of world-class managers such as Xabi Alonso, who he faced last season when Alonso was in charge of Real Madrid.

In the goalless draw with Real Madrid at Vallecas in November, Chavarria produced an excellent defensive performance - showing the aggression and discipline required to deal with elite attacking players.

His performance left an impression on Alonso and Chavarria became a key target for the Spanish coach after he was appointed Chelsea manager.

He also started for Rayo in last season's Conference League final, where they suffered a 1-0 defeat by Crystal Palace.

Alongside new right-back Marco Palestra, who joined Chelsea for £47m from Atalanta in July, Chavarria's arrival gives Alonso the chance to replicate his wing-back system that helped Bayer Leverkusen win the Bundesliga title in 2024.

His signing also adds depth to the left-back position after Marc Cucurella joined Real Madrid in June for £51.8m.

Getting the deal over the line has not been easy for Chelsea, who were initially told by Rayo Vallecano that they would not sell Chavarria unless his release clause, now worth £42.4m, was met.

Talks were described as "complicated" by multiple BBC Sport sources after Rayo made it clear they wanted the release clause paid in full.

They believed the price was justified, with sources at the club arguing that Chavarria's underlying statistics show he plays at a similar level to Cucurella.

He scored once last season and made three assists in all competitions, creating 27 chances from open play in La Liga.

Furthermore, Chavarria had four years remaining on his contract and Rayo's successful player-trading model has left the club in a strong financial position, allowing them to resist offers in a similar way to Spain's traditional big three of Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

That profitability also means Rayo would be liable for a 25% tax charge on any additional profit generated from a sale, reducing the net value of any fee received.

title: I owe Villa the world but Man Utd are above them - Tielemans
description: Manchester United new boy Youri Tielemans gives his first extended interview on his £35m dream move, making it third time lucky for the ex-Aston Villa man.
fullText:
It was third time lucky this summer in the history of Youri Tielemans and Manchester United.

United looked seriously at the Belgium midfielder in 2019, after Tielemans had impressed in an initial loan spell at Leicester. And again in 2022, as they spent too long holding out for Frenkie de Jong to decide if he was prepared to leave Barcelona.

But it was this July, while the 29-year-old was on World Cup duty, when the Old Trafford outfit made their move, triggering a £35m release clause to snap Tielemans up on a five-year deal from Aston Villa.

"There had been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve anything," he recalled.

"I was very calm. I was not expecting much this summer, to be fair. I was just focused on my football, focused on the World Cup and trying to perform my best for my country.

"But you know every summer something can happen and obviously I was aware of the clause.

"I am very thankful to Aston Villa. I owe them the world. It is a great club, we did amazing things and they have put me back to my best level. But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.

"It is a great achievement for any footballer to end up here. It means you have done well in your career. But it does not end there. I want to be successful."

Tielemans cameo against PSG hints at Man Utd future

Man Utd sign Tielemans for £35m from Aston Villa

Tielemans cuts a relaxed figure as he conducts his first extended media interview since his switch from Villa, taking time to personally shake hands with all the journalists present.

He positively beams at points, noticeably when he is asked whether – given he scored Leicester's winner in the 2021 FA Cup final and then the opener for Villa in their Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May – if he can bring goals to Manchester United.

It is also clear from his expression a partnership with skipper Bruno Fernandes is developing.

Senior Manchester United officials noticed it in Gothenburg last weekend, even though the pair were only on the pitch together for 26 minutes in the 1-1 draw with Paris St-Germain.

"It's really natural," he said. "He is a guy that can find space easily. I just try and find him so that he can move forward."

Tielemans is thoughtful though, and expansive in his answers, even if sometimes what he says is not quite what you expect to hear.

One of those is around the length of his career and the number of games he has played.

He made his professional debut for Anderlecht at 16. He has played 668 games for club and country and had to pull out of Belgium's World Cup quarter-final clash with Spain last month after experiencing an issue in the warm-up.

"I feel very good, actually," he said.

"In that last game, it was just an overload of too many games; too many minutes. Unfortunately, my body could not cope with it anymore.

"We played 120 minutes against Senegal, then played the US a few days later, three days after that we played against Spain.

"In the warm-up, my body just switched off for some reason.

"I do not think I am a player that absolutely needs a rest. Obviously, there are a lot of games, and the manager needs to manage the team, but when I am good, I am good.

"When it does not go well, I will know straight away and I will alert the manager. But it does not happen often."

While Tielemans is new to Manchester United, there are some familiar faces helping him to settle in.

Chief among them is Jonny Evans, a former team-mate at Leicester. The pair have remained close and Evans offered a positive character reference to head coach Michael Carrick.

Tielemans also played with Harry Maguire for a short period at Leicester, and Marcus Rashford was a team-mate at Aston Villa.

To the surprise of many, including himself probably, Rashford is back at his boyhood club, having initially left for Villa under a cloud after his fall-out with Ruben Amorim.

"He was great," said Tielemans.

"There had been so much talk about him, bringing pressure and the media around him, but he was so good.

"He was very humble and hard-working, and from the first training session you could tell his touch and acceleration was just amazing. That was what we needed at the time. He did many good things and hopefully he can bring them here."

It could be argued Tielemans' arrival addresses an issue Manchester United has had since Carrick quit in 2018; the scheming midfielder with an eye for a pass, who can break a defensive line.

In theory, it will allow Fernandes more room further forward and offer the opportunity to control games for a team that has, in recent times, tended to be viewed as being better on the counter-attack.

Tielemans had a brief chat with Carrick before he completed his move.

But the past 10 days have offered a great insight into Carrick's expectations.

"He wants me to be free on the pitch, to try and organise the team the best I can," he said.

"He has got his structure. He wants to have the ball and wants to press in certain ways.

"It might be different than what I am used to, but it is logical things in my opinion.

"It is just smelling football, which is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht, you know.

"For me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together."

title: Failed presidential candidate wins Dem primary for Midwest governor amid fraud scandal fallout
description: Amy Klobuchar defeated long-shot challengers in the Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party primary as she seeks to replace Tim Walz amid a $9 billion fraud scandal.
fullText:
Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., has won the Democratic nomination for governor of Minnesota as she continues her bid to replace outgoing Gov. Tim Walz, who dropped out of his re-election bid in the midst of a massive fraud scandal.

Klobuchar, Minnesota's senior U.S. senator and a former Democratic presidential candidate, defeated a field of long-shot challengers in Tuesday's Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party primary.

Klobuchar will move on to face the winner of the crowded GOP primary in November.

Mn Governor Race To Replace Walz Sees Major Shakeup As Gop Contender Ends Campaign: 'Don't See A Path'

Walz announced earlier this year that he would not seek another term as governor as his administration faced intense criticism over its handling of fraud involving Minnesota government programs that federal prosecutors say could end up costing the taxpayers over $9 billion.

The fraud issue has loomed over Minnesota politics, with Republicans hammering Walz and state Democrats over what they say was a failure to prevent the misuse of taxpayer dollars.

Klobuchar entered the race with significant advantages in name recognition and political experience. She has represented Minnesota in the Senate since 2007 and previously served as Hennepin County attorney.

She also sought the Democratic presidential nomination in 2020 before ending her campaign and endorsing former President Joe Biden.

Klobuchar Vows Fraud Crackdown, Audit Of Mn Gov't As Gop Blasts Walz Ties

When she rolled out her governing priorities in May, Klobuchar said: "You are right to be angry about the fraud. It is unacceptable and it must end." She promised a "top-to-bottom audit" of state government beginning on "day one."

The Plymouth, Minnesota born Klobuchar's campaign includes a policy plank titled "Make Government Accountable and Root out Fraud." It says that "fixing the government is the foundation of everything we need to do" and promises "immediate action to root out fraud."

Klobuchar's gubernatorial campaign puts her in the unusual position of seeking a new office without first relinquishing her seat in Washington.

Klobuchar has not resigned from the Senate while campaigning for governor. Her current Senate term does not expire until January 2031, meaning a loss in the gubernatorial race would not by itself cost her the Senate seat.

If Klobuchar wins the governorship in November and resigns from the Senate, her departure would create a vacancy in Minnesota's congressional delegation.

Klobuchar will now attempt to keep the governor's mansion in Democratic hands in November in a state that has not had a Republican governor since former Gov. Tim Pawlenty left office in January 2011.

title: Dangerous drug-resistant fungus spreads across US, reaching 27 states
description: Thousands of Candida auris cases have been reported across 27 states in 2026, with the drug-resistant fungus posing deadly risks in healthcare settings.
fullText:
Thousands of cases of a potentially deadly, drug-resistant fungus have been reported across 27 states so far this year, according to provisional CDC data.

As of the week ending July 25, a total of 3,437 clinical cases of Candida auris (C. auris) had been documented in the U.S. so far in 2026.

California accounts for 873 cases — roughly one-quarter of the country's total. Other states with high numbers include Texas (433), Tennessee (283), Ohio (279), Georgia (193), Louisiana (179), Illinois (171), Arizona (171), Michigan (146), Virginia (132) and Pennsylvania (121), per the CDC.

Experts Reveal How To Avoid Deadly Legionnaires' Disease As Nyc Outbreak Kills 5

The remaining states have fewer than 100 cases each.

Candida auris is a type of yeast that can cause serious infections, primarily in hospitals, nursing homes and other healthcare settings.

The fungus, which can survive on surfaces for prolonged periods, is "highly transmissible between patients through contact with contaminated surfaces or objects," the CDC states. It can spread through contaminated items such as bedrails, doorknobs and shared medical equipment.

C. auris can also be spread by people who carry the fungus but do not show symptoms, known as "colonization."

Clinical cases do not necessarily represent infections. The CDC defines a clinical case as detection of C. auris in a specimen collected during the normal course of medical care.

Some clinical specimens can come from sites where the presence of C. auris may represent colonization rather than a true infection.

The health effects of the fungus can range from colonization without symptoms to potentially deadly invasive infections, including bloodstream infections.

Those most at risk of infection include patients with severe underlying medical conditions. In particular, those who use breathing tubes, feeding tubes, IVs or catheters are more vulnerable, as are those who are hospitalized frequently or for long periods of time.

People without those risk factors are unlikely to become colonized with C. auris or develop an infection.

Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst and clinical professor of medicine at NYU Langone, said he considers C. auris an "emerging problem of great concern."

Click Here For More Health Stories

"It is resistant to multiple antifungal drugs, and it tends to spread in hospital settings, including on equipment being used on immunocompromised and semi-immunocompromised patients, such as ventilators and catheters," he previously told Fox News Digital.

"Unfortunately, symptoms such as fever, chills and aches may be ubiquitous, and it can be mistaken for other infections."

Invasive C. auris infections have been associated with mortality rates of 30% to 72%, although most affected patients are already seriously ill. This can make it difficult to determine how often the fungus is a direct cause of death.

Candida auris can be difficult to treat because it is often resistant to antifungal medications, leading the CDC to classify the fungus as an "urgent antimicrobial-resistance threat."

Test Yourself With Our Latest Lifestyle Quiz

More than 90% of U.S. samples are resistant to fluconazole, a common antifungal treatment. Echinocandins, another family of antifungals, are currently the main treatment option for C. auris, although some strains are resistant to all three main classes of antifungals.

"Major research" is ongoing to develop new treatments, according to Siegel.

"This is part of a much larger problem of emerging antibiotic resistance in the U.S. and around the world," the physician previously cautioned. "At the same time, sterilization and disinfection measures in hospitals can be very helpful."

Fox News Digital's Angelica Stabile contributed reporting.
