title: Trump doesn't dismiss declaring national emergency to restrict voting
description: "Stranger things have happened," Trump said when an interviewer suggested he declare a national emergency to take executive action on voting.
fullText:
President Donald Trump isn't dismissing the possibility that he could declare a national security emergency in an attempt to establish new voting restrictions stalled in the Senate, telling an interviewer that "stranger things have happened."

Trump has spent weeks hammering senators to pass the SAVE America Act, legislation that would require proof of citizenship to register to vote and a photo ID when casting a ballot.

The bill is Trump's top legislative priority, but it has struggled to attract enough support in the Senate, and lawmakers left for their August recess last week without passing it.

During a Real America's Voice interview with Trump on Aug. 10, host Wayne Allyn Root suggested declaring a national emergency to implement voting changes, a move that almost certainly would be challenged in court.

"Let me put an idea in your head, OK?" Root said, adding: "If they never get the SAVE America Act done, you have the right to declare a national security emergency for elections … so if you do this in the next month we will get photo ID, proof of citizenship and a limit to mail-in ballots and you don't even need the Senate's vote."

"Let me just say that stranger things have happened, OK?" Trump interjected. "I'll leave it at that."

The comments come as Trump has taken steps to assert greater federal authority over elections, which are administered by state and local officials. Trump suggested earlier this year that Republicans should "nationalize" the voting process, generating bipartisan pushback and alarming opponents who worried about the fairness of future contests.

"Donald Trump wants to take over American elections," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-New York, said in response to Trump's remarks to Root.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The president issued an executive order in March that moved to exert federal control over voter rolls and mail-in ballots. Trump directed the Department of Homeland Security to develop lists of eligible voters in each state and ordered the U.S. Postal Service to only deliver ballots to voters on the approved lists.

The move escalated Trump's bid to place new restrictions on voting ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, when control of Congress is at stake. It was quickly challenged in court by Democrat-led states, and on June 25 a federal judge in Boston blocked the order.

The Trump administration filed an emergency appeal to the Supreme Court on July 27 seeking permission to implement two provisions in the order. The states that brought the lawsuit responded in a court filing that there would be "extraordinary consequences" from allowing the order to proceed.

Trump has argued that new voting rules are needed to safeguard elections as he makes unfounded claims about widespread voter fraud. Democrats and voting rights groups say the SAVE America Act would disenfranchise millions of eligible voters.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Trump doesn't dismiss declaring national emergency to restrict voting

title: Tiffany Haddish avoids more jail time by pleading guilty to a drunk driving charge in Georgia
description: Actor and comedian Tiffany Haddish avoided additional jail time Tuesday when she pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor alcohol-related driving charge that stemmed from her 2022 arrest in Georgia after someo...
fullText:
FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. (AP) — Actor and comedian Tiffany Haddish avoided additional jail time Tuesday when she pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor alcohol-related driving charge that stemmed from her 2022 arrest in Georgia after someone called 911 about a driver asleep at the wheel at a traffic light.

Other charges were dropped. After entering the plea by video, Haddish was placed on 12 months' probation and told to avoid drugs and alcohol and complete a substance abuse evaluation. She was credited for the brief time she spent in jail following her arrest.

Haddish's films include the comedy "Girls Trip," "Night School," "Like a Boss" and "The Kitchen." She wrote the New York Times bestseller "The Last Black Unicorn," which earned a Grammy nomination for a subsequent audiobook she narrated. In 2018, she won an Emmy for her appearance on "Saturday Night Live" and a Grammy in 2021 for her special "Black Mitzvah."

At around 2:30 a.m. on Jan. 14, 2022, someone called 911 to report seeing a person who appeared to be asleep in the driver's seat of a white Ford Explorer with their foot on the brake in Peachtree City, about 30 miles (48 kilometers) south of Atlanta, according to a court filing. An officer spotted an SUV that matched the description given by the caller and stopped Haddish as she pulled into a neighborhood, according to a police report.

Haddish's lawyers in May asked a judge to dismiss the case, arguing that waiting more than four years for the case to be resolved had caused personal and professional difficulties and violated her right to a speedy trial. Fayette County State Court Judge Jason Thompson rejected her arguments.

The judge found that Haddish and her attorneys had requested some of the delays, including a request for a delay so she could attend a fashion show in Morocco and a request to leave a hearing early to catch a flight. He wrote that she also did not show any evidence of having missed specific performing opportunities or of actual financial harm because of the delay.

Haddish also was arrested in November 2023 in Beverly Hills, California, on suspicion of driving under the influence after police received a call and said Haddish appeared to be slumped over the wheel of a vehicle while the engine was still running.

Haddish reached a plea deal with prosecutors in that case in February 2024, pleading no contest to a vehicle code violation, and the two misdemeanor DUI charges against her were dropped, according to the Los Angeles Times.

title: The First Five Things You Should Do With Your Garmin Cirqa Smart Band
description: Make the most of Garmin's first screenless smart band right from the start.
fullText:
The Garmin Cirqa is the company’s first screen-free smart band, built to track fitness and wellness features around the clock, without needing a subscription. For existing Garmin fans who want 24/7 data without wearing a bulky sports watch to bed, this $199 smart band is a welcome addition. If you just unboxed one, here's how to get it set up right and start making the most of it.

If you already own a Garmin watch like a Fenix or Forerunner, you can still keep your watch as your "Primary Training Device." But for round-the-clock daily health metrics, assign the Cirqa your "Primary Wearable." If you missed this during your initial set-up, here's how to manage your devices in the Garmin Connect app:

Scroll to the bottom of the page and select Settings.

Under Device Priority, select the Cirqa for Primary Wearable, and a different watch for Primary Training Device.

This setup makes sure your Cirqa’s continuous collection of recovery metrics, step counts, and sleep data flow into your profile, while preventing the smart band from conflicting with your primary sports watch during hard workouts.

The Cirqa’s fabric wristband comes in two sizes. The small/medium fits wrist circumferences of about 120–200 mm, while the large/extra-large fits roughly 145–240 mm. A snug-but-comfortable fit matters for accurate optical heart rate readings, so take a minute to adjust the strap before you start relying on the numbers.

Garmin sells an upper-arm band separately for $49.99, so if you'd rather track from your bicep than your wrist, that's an option worth exploring—especially if you do activities where a wrist-worn band gets in the way. Plus, upper arm placement might improve your heart rate accuracy overall, since it gives the sensor better contact with a meatier part of the body with less wrist-movement noise.

The Connect app's insights can seem a bit scattered and overwhelming at first, so don't feel like you need to absorb everything on day one. The Cirqa can track training readiness, HRV status, VO2 max, heart rate, Pulse Ox, stress, sleep tracking, and more. Within sleep tracking, you can track sleep stages (although those are dubious), naps, and personalized coaching layered on top of your basic sleep score.

Your watch comes preloaded with glances, but you can customize these based on your goals. For instance, I find Garmin's Body Battery to be an overly simplified and ultimately unhelpful score. Since I'm training for a marathon, I replaced that glance with my Running Economy score, so I can readily track how I'm improving as I increase my running volume and intensity.

If it's relevant to you, this is also the moment to set up women's health tracking. The Cirqa estimates period predictions and past ovulation windows using skin temperature data gathered while you sleep, and it can sync that data to the Natural Cycles birth control app (which requires its own separate subscription).

Something to keep in mind: Some of the richer insights (like training readiness trends or sleep coaching) take several days or weeks of data to become meaningful. Give it a week or two of normal wear before you judge what it's telling you.

Compared to other smart bands, the Cirqa's on-device button really sets it apart. The Cirqa can track more than 80 activities—running, yoga, cycling and more—either by pressing the button or through the Garmin Connect app. It allegedly detects workouts automatically, but I’ve found that to be pretty unreliable.

To make the most of this feature, you want to assign which activity type you want to start and stop with a quick press of the button. Head to your Garmin Connect app and select the Cirqa in the top right corner. Then select Activity Options > Edit (in the top right corner) > Select your favorite activity. Now, when you press the button on your Cirqa, it'll start your favorite activity type.

And if you're heading outside, remember the band pairs with your phone's GPS for accurate location tracking during outdoor activities, since the Cirqa itself (like most smart bands) has no onboard GPS receiver—so bring your phone along if logging your route matters to you.

Beyond the headline fitness and sleep features, the Cirqa packs in a handful of lifestyle tools worth checking out. The app includes a Jet Lag Adviser, lifestyle logging and journaling, hydration and calorie tracking, daily step counts, and intensity minutes. There's also a wheelchair mode for wrist-based push tracking, if that fits your activity style.

In general, it's worth taking the time to really familiarize yourself with the Garmin Connect app. Remember, the Cirqa has no screen, so for every insight you want to see, you'll need to know where to find it in the app. And since we're in the early days of this smart band's launch, the app is where you'll want to regularly check for firmware updates.

title: The Best Way to Get Past an Article's Paywall
description: Some tricks that used to work no longer do—but this one is pretty reliable.
fullText:
The era of the free internet is long over: As the online ad market has collapsed in recent years, largely thanks to changes Google has made to forefront AI summaries, countless websites have added paywalls. This means if you want to read their articles, you have to sign up and pay a monthly subscription fee. Some sites have a “metered” paywall—meaning you can read a certain number of articles for free before they ask for money—and others have a hard paywall, where you’ll have to pay to read even one article.

Paywalls are mostly a thing with news websites, largely because relying on advertising income alone isn’t a viable strategy anymore, forcing these companies to pursue direct revenue sources like monthly subscriptions. In that sense, paywalls aren't a bad thing—it’s wonderful to support journalism you find valuable. If nothing else, I hope you support the websites that you read regularly—especially your local news outlet.

But sometimes, you just need to get around a paywall quickly. Maybe you've lost your password, haven’t saved it on your phone, are in a rush, or are strapped for cash and swear to yourself that you’ll subscribe later. If one of these exceptions applies, there are many ways to bypass paywalls on the internet—though not nearly as many as there used to be.

Many once-reliable methods of bypassing paywalls have stopped working almost entirely (pour one out for pasting the headline into Google and opening the link in a private browsing window). The methods discussed below are more robust—and thus, more likely to work. I'll start with my favorite, which has served me well for the past few years. But a word of caution: You may be able to use one of these methods successfully today, but that could change in the future as websites clamp down on bypass methods. (This article is regularly updated as some methods stop working and others pop up.)

Archive.today is the fastest, most reliable way I've found to quickly bypass a paywall, and I've been using it successfully for years across a wide range of sites, even as other options have come and gone. It's a site that will create an archived version of any website you paste into the search bar. (Think of an archived version like taking a screenshot of any website, complete with a time stamp—a self-described “time capsule,” if you will.) Archive.today “saves a text and a graphical copy of the page for better accuracy” and gives you a short link to an unalterable record of any web page. Yes, yes—but as a bonus, you can often use this functionality to bypass a paywall and read an entire paywalled article without issue. 

Just paste your article link into the black “I want to search the archive for saved snapshots” bar, and you'll be taken to a page where you can view earlier archived versions. If the article you’re trying to bypass isn’t already archived, then put the URL into the red “My URL is alive and I want to archive its content” bar. The site will then begin generating the archived version, which usually only takes a few minutes. You'll be sent straight to this archived version once it's ready, and you can come back to it later by copying the new URL from your browser's nav bar.

You can also add a browser extension to Chrome that will create a button in your browser toolbar you can click to instantly create an archived snapshot of any web page. The archived version will even automatically open up in a new tab.

I've only had this site fail me once or twice. Usually, there's already an existing archived version for anything I want to read, but creating a new one only takes a minute or two. Still, if it doesn't work, try the next option.

A newer tool I found while poking around "get around a paywall" Reddit, smry.ai is a tool that works similarly to Archive.today, in that it shows you a cached version of the article page (pulled, according to the developer, from either the Internet Wayback Machine or Google cache), which allows you to read the entire thing. What sets this one apart is AI integration: Click the purple "generate" button on the results page to get an AI-generated summary of the article's key points. In practice, I found the summaries to be more akin to social media posts than an outline (for example, a 7,000-word New York Magazine article about the recent assassination attempts on the life of former President Donald Trump was trimmed to a single short paragraph), but if you're just looking for the gist—or trying to decide if you want to read the entire article at all—it's a nice little addition.

If you're willing to try solutions that are a little more technical than a mere copy and paste, one of these options might work for you.

Some websites use JavaScript to hide content behind paywalls, and you can circumvent those blocks by disabling JavaScript in your browser. Note that disabling JavaScript can (and will) break most websites—some may not let you view comments, while others may not load at all. But it’s worth trying if you just need to read the content of the post.

Ideally, you’d use a separate browser for this so that you don’t have to keep enabling and disabling JavaScript. Once you’ve chosen your secondary browser, check out our guide to disabling JavaScript in various ones.

Some paywalled sites, like The Washington Post, will let you read a limited number of articles for free each month, then throw up the wall once you've hit the limit. You can use a VPN to change up your IP address and trick the site into giving you more freebies. This method won't help you on sites that don't offer any free access, but it's worth trying, and will work with both paid and free VPNs.

If you understand a bit of HTML and CSS, you can edit elements using your browser to go past some paywalls. Essentially, you’re editing the page to remove the banners that lock content behind a subscription. It’s a lot like opening the curtains to reveal the nice view outside your window.

It works with some websites, but others have added a hard block that reveals the article only if you’ve signed in with a paid account. Still, it’s worth trying once to see if it works:

On any website, right-click the banner just below the last visible sentence of the article and select Inspect Element. This will open up a console where you can search for the offending elements and hide or change them. The exact element varies from site to site, but it’s often labeled display, paywall, or subscribe. Here’s a neat GIF on Reddit that shows you how to get it done.

If you are trying to read a paywalled article on an Android phone, you can get around it with the Bypass Paywalls Clean browser extension. This extension used to be available for Firefox but has been removed from the Mozilla store. However, you can add it to a different browser; Reddit users recommend trying the Kiwi browser.

The last method on our list works only on iPhones: Apple’s free Shortcuts app lets you run automation routines on your iPhone, and its tools have been used to bypass paywalls on various websites. There are plenty of these shortcuts, and they may all not work with all websites. Get started by trying Bypass Paywall or Unpaywall.

Many libraries offer access to paid magazine and newspaper subscriptions online. Typically you'll have to go to your library's website, log in with your card number or account details, and then access different publications indirectly, via the library's portal. (For example, if you live in Marin County, Calif., you can easily read the Washington Post for free.)

There are too many library systems out there to count, so you may or may not be lucky enough to be in one that offers this perk, but it's worth a shot; since the library is paying the publication for the service, you don't even need to feel guilty. (Not sure if your system has a news portal? Ask your local librarian!)

This one isn't likely to be feasible often, but it's worth a shot for when you're trying to read that one paywalled article that's going viral: Many publications allow paid subscribers to "gift" a copy of a certain number of articles every month (The Washington Post and the New York Times each allow gifting 10 articles per month, for example). If you know your aunt subscribes to The New York Times, it can't hurt to ask if she's willing to gift you the occasional read.

title: Five New Changes in iOS 27 Beta 5
description: Apple's latest test build of iOS 27 has some small but worthwhile updates.
fullText:
Apple released the fifth beta for iOS 27 on Monday, Aug. 10. As we get closer to the update's official fall release, the number of features and changes Apple will introduce with each beta is certainly diminishing, and no one would call beta 5 a feature-filled update. However, there are some new features and changes worth noting, especially as they are things Apple didn't previously announce at WWDC. 

Before I get into what's new, a reminder: iOS 27 is not yet finished. As such, while anyone with a compatible iPhone can install it, know there are risks to running beta software on your device. Make sure to make a proper backup of your data, as you could lose everything on your iPhone in the event you need to downgrade back to iOS 26.

When you update your iPhone to the latest iOS 27 beta—or, presumably, iOS 27 itself—you're going to notice new icons for some familiar apps. Some updates are quite subtle, such as Safari. You might not even notice at first, since the icon retains the same basic design as before, but with this latest beta, Safari now has fewer "ticks" in its compass than before, a slightly different blue background, and a distinct screw in its center. It reminds me a bit of iOS 7's flat design. It's the same story for Settings and the App Store icons: small adjustments that you might not notice without comparing the icons side by side.

If you've been running the beta, you'll notice the update to the Siri app right away. Instead of the colorful, looping logo Apple debuted with the app, Siri now appears as a gray, glowing orb. Preview's new app icon is also readily apparent: replacing the loupe against a blue background, the new logo places the loop in the bottom-right corner of a colorful, rounded square. I'm personally a fan of these changes, especially for Preview.

If you have a compatible iPhone, you can customize how Siri AI sounds through a new feature called "enhanced voice." With it, you can change both Siri's pace and expressivity to make a voice that's a bit more unique to your iPhone than others. With the first four iOS 27 betas, enhanced voice only worked with various American English accents. But starting with iOS 27 beta 5, Apple now supports customizing British English voices as well. According to 9to5Mac, you now have 11 different voices to customize.

Dive into the Settings after updating your iPhone, and you'll find a new option in the "Search Settings" menu. "Before Searching" comes with three new settings. The biggest change is "Suggest Apps," which lets you choose how many suggested apps appear in Siri Suggestions (the default is eight). There's also "Suggest App Shortcuts," which appears to let you choose whether or not iOS suggests app shortcuts, and "Show Recent Searches," which lets you hide your searches from this menu.

As reported by Apple Insider, iOS 27 beta 5 will tell you when you installed your current version of iOS on your iPhone. I'm not sure exactly in what scenarios this would be useful, but it's a new change.

Here's a small but interesting change: Apple is no longer showing cellular network types while you're on wifi. If you check Control Center, you won't see whether you're connected to LTE, 5G, or something like 5G UWB as long as you're connected to wifi as well. You'll need to jump off the wifi to see what cellular network your iPhone is connected to. (For what it's worth, I currently can't see my cellular network type while connected to wifi on iOS 26 either, but maybe that's a carrier thing, as I'm seeing multiple reports about this change.)

title: Maresca on Guardiola, captaincy dilemma & AI masterclasses
description: New Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca talks about replacing Pep Guardiola, his interest in AI and his captaincy dilemma.
fullText:
How do you replace Pep Guardiola?

Enzo Maresca is just starting to find out this summer, having been chosen as the Spaniard's successor at Manchester City - returning after being Guardiola's assistant during the club's Treble-winning 2022-23 campaign.

Guardiola, one of the greatest managers of his generation, stepped down at the end of last season after leading City to 17 major trophies, including six Premier League titles and a Champions League victory.

Now, with his first pre-season as manager at the club nearing its end, Maresca sat down with the five travelling UK-based media in Seoul to discuss the challenges ahead.

"After 10 games, if we have got 10 points, 20 points, 30 points. People will be comparing it to Pep after 10 games, it doesn't put pressure on me," said Maresca.

"I have said many times while I was at Leicester or Chelsea, he is the best manager in the world over the last 15 or 20 years.

"When he started in Spain, everyone wanted to play like Barcelona, he moved to Germany everyone wanted to play like Bayern [Munich], he comes to England and everyone wants to play like City.

"Someone asked me if it's the impossible job to follow him - maybe, but at the same time it's a privilege."

The ex-Chelsea boss says he met Guardiola in Barcelona a day before he officially signed as his replacement, as it was "useful" to pick his brains - having been at the club for a decade.

"We spent some hours together," he said. "We had planned before the season finished here to spend some time in the summer holidays together.

"I like to go in empty sometimes to see things for myself - but he was here so long, he has his opinions. But also you have to arrive and see things for yourself, see all the picture."

To signal a change for the players, Maresca has moved into the office of former assistant Pep Lijnders at City's headquarters, next door to Guardiola's old office - which has now been converted into a meeting room.

Shortly after his appointment as the City boss at the end of June, Maresca apologised to former club Chelsea for the "disruption" caused by his mid-season departure.

So what did he do during the intervening six months?

"I tried to enjoy a little bit more [time] with the family," he says about his wife and four children.

"And everyone is talking about AI, so I want to understand how it works. So I did two masterclasses to understand it a little bit more and have more knowledge."

Such has been the rise of artificial intelligence in everyday life, even Premier League managers are now beginning to dabble in it for those marginal gains.

But Maresca is going to need more than AI to make a success of his City career, having taken over from one of the greatest managers of his generation.

Marmoush double as Man City beat Atletico in Seoul

Man City reject Barcelona's £38.5m bid for Rodri

Maresca says the biggest difference in the Premier League from three years ago, when he was assistant to Guardiola, is the rise in set-pieces and teams defending man-to-man.

Last season, Arsenal claimed their first top-flight crown in more than two decades and scored 25 goals from set-pieces in the process - including 19 from corners alone - which is one aspect City are looking to "try to improve".

But rules for next season have been brought in, in an attempt to speed up the game - such as players having five seconds for goal-kicks and throw-ins, with possession handed over to the opposition if those limits are exceeded.

Despite the look of crowded penalty areas and jostling at corners seemingly taking away from the division stylistically, Maresca still feels it is the "best league" with the "best players".

He says: "It is because of the quality of the players, the quality of the managers, the organisation of the Premier League. It is completely different compared to other countries.

"Which league can compete with the Premier League? Spain? Barcelona, Real Madrid, yes, but then the rest is not the same. You have six teams here who are more or less there."

Maresca said he has not done an initiation song in front of the squad as "the manager doesn't sing".

He described goalkeeping coach Michele de Bernardin's performance as being "very good", while analyst Javi Molina's rendition of Frank Sinatra's My Way was "the worst".

The make-up of the backroom staff - with Argentine Willy Caballero, two Italians, three Spaniards and Maresca being able to speak French - means they have plenty of languages covered.

And then there is "the Englishman" - first-team coach Danny Walker, who was Maresca's assistant in City's elite development squad (EDS) and followed him to Leicester and Chelsea.

The manager is beaming when he discusses Walker. He says: "We go for breakfast it is beans on toast, we go for dinner it is a beer.

"When I joined the EDS, Danny was there, he was previously with the under-16s and they moved him to become my assistant. Since then we are always together, he knows Nico O'Reilly, Rico Lewis, he had them from under-six to under-12. He knows all of them.

"He is very good. He is good on extra work at the end, when we keep players doing something extra.

"It is demanding. If we don't win games, we are all going home."

Speaking of Englishmen, Maresca will choose the next City captain himself after Bernardo Silva's departure, and wants a homegrown player in the committee.

The leadership group currently consists of frontrunner Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland and Rodri, who has been the subject of a failed bid from Barcelona.

So is the Norway star a leading candidate to take the armband?

"Erling was one of the first to send a message when I joined the club," said Maresca.

"At Leicester and Chelsea I had a rule that when we scored the captain had to come to the bench, not to celebrate, but for instructions. But if he scores, then he can celebrate.

"If Erling is the captain, we have a problem, can you imagine? If you saw the game [against K-League XI] on Wednesday, when we scored the first goal, Ruben came over to the bench.

"I think even if it is two or three minutes, there is always something to adjust. At the moment, we have three or four [in the leadership group] and we are missing one. In the case of Rodri, see what happens."

The next captain, Rodri's future, City's starting XI for Sunday's Community Shield against Arsenal - the big decisions are stacking up as Maresca begins to settle into one of the biggest jobs on the planet.

title: Rangers' Chermiti out for 'significant period' with knee injury
description: Youssef Chermiti faces a long recovery from anterior cruciate ligament damage sustained shortly after Rangers turned down an offer for the striker.
fullText:
Youssef Chermiti faces a long recovery from anterior cruciate ligament damage sustained shortly after Rangers turned down an offer for the striker.

The 22-year-old Portuguese was injured during Sunday's 2-1 home defeat to Hibernian as he collided with advertising boards following a jarring challenge.

A club announcement via social media states Chermiti "will be out of action for a significant period of time".

He moved to Ibrox from Everton in September 2025, reportedly becoming Rangers' most expensive purchase since Tore Andre Flo in 2000.

Capped at under-21 level by Portugal, the centre forward has made 43 Rangers appearances, 30 of them starts, scoring 15 goals.

At Monday's shareholders' meeting, chairman Andrew Cavenagh was quizzed about the wisdom of Chermiti playing amid transfer interest.

The American replied: "Just because someone lobs an unsolicited offer in on one sheet of paper, you don't yank a player from a really important match."

Prior to kick-off on Sunday, manager Derek McInnes was asked to comment on reports that Turkish champions Galatasaray were the interested club and told BBC Scotland: "I'm led to believe the club's valuation of the player hasn't been met.

"It's no surprise that he's a player who's got a big (price) tag on him and he's got high potential, but thankfully he's our player and that will continue to be the case.

"We're trying to build a team here at the minute and we're trying to still bring additions to the team that helps us add to the good players that we've got, including Youssef.

"So it's not something we would encourage at any point."

Rangers chairman expects up to five more signings

Chermiti injured after Rangers reject bid for striker

What is an ACL injury and why is it so serious?

From my vantage point in the main stand at Ibrox, I winced as soon as I saw Chermiti crumple into a heap behind Raphael Sallinger's goal.

He immediately raised his arm, signalling he was in agony and that he needed urgent attention. It was instantly clear his game was over. What Rangers will now be hoping is his entire season isn't finished.

A cruciate ligament injury is by definition a serious one. The fact the club are already signalling he's out for a "significant period" tells its own story.

The timing could not have been worse and McInnes will be starting to wonder if the early days of his tenure at Ibrox are jinxed. On the very day Rangers turned down a substantial bid - reported to be £22m - for Chermiti, he suffers an injury that will rule him out for months.

The board had a decision to make: look to bank a significant deal and rest him against Hibs or reject the "unsolicited" offer and play him. If they could turn back time...

Chairman Cavenagh says "three to five" new faces will still be recruited, and that will be music to McInnes' ears. He may now need a new striker, with Chermiti out.

Lawrence Shankland is still to get his Rangers career off the mark and Ryan Naderi doesn't look like the answer to the team's current lack of goals. Bojan Miovski is still on the books but is yet to play a competitive minute for his new manager.

McInnes started Chermiti in both of the past two matches but must now find the goals to see off Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok in Europa League qualifying without him.

title: Pogba expected to have Monaco contract terminated
description: Paul Pogba is expected to leave Monaco amid talks over a possible contract termination.
fullText:
Paul Pogba is expected to leave Monaco amid talks over a possible contract termination.

The former World Cup winner joined the Ligue 1 side last summer after he was permitted to return to professional football after a doping suspension.

Pogba signed a two year deal, which was due to run until the end of the forthcoming season.

But a source has told the BBC discussions over an early exit are under way and are expected to be concluded soon.

Monaco have not yet commented on the situation.

Pogba's first season at Monaco was disrupted by injury but there was hope this season would see the France international play regularly.

But a change in manager, after Filipe Luis replaced Sebastien Pocognoli, could see Monaco head in a different direction in central midfield.

Pogba was provisionally banned from football for four years after a positive test for dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in February 2024, following a doping test in August 2023.

Pogba maintained it was a mistake and that he was given a supplement without knowing it contained a banned substance.

The France international, a 2018 World Cup winner, was permitted to return to football in March 2025 following the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision to reduce his ban to 18 months.

title: Bath in 'serious discussions' to play in Reading
description: Reading owner Rob Couhig says the club have had "serious discussions" with Bath about the Prem Rugby club playing at their stadium.
fullText:
Bath have had "serious discussions" about playing two of their 2026-27 games at Reading's Select Car Leasing Stadium, Royals owner Rob Couhig has said.

Bath confirmed they will play their final two home games of the Prem season away from the Recreation Ground to enable construction work to begin as part of a redevelopment.

Couhig, who took over as Reading owner in May 2025, said the League One club have had talks with Bath but would not disclose how far they have progressed.

"The stadium is well equipped for it, they would be foolish to not try and pursue us," the American told BBC Radio Berkshire.

A Bath spokesperson said: "Discussions with a number of venues are still ongoing and we will confirm our alternative location in due course."

Bath to go on the road for Prem season run-in

Champions Saints host Newcastle on opening weekend

Bath's games against Harlequins on the weekend of 15 May and Saracens on 5 June are scheduled to be moved, and if the club were to reach the Prem semi-finals and secure a home tie next June, that fixture would also be played away from the Rec.

The club's owners say the plans are being accelerated to ensure the redevelopment is completed for the start of the 2028-29 Prem campaign.

Reading's final home game of the upcoming season is against Sheffield Wednesday on 1 May. However, they would be due to host another match that month if they reach the League One play-offs.

Their ground has been regularly used for rugby in the past, having been the home of London Irish between 2000 to 2020.

Couhig highlighted a number of changes and upgrades which have been made at the SCL Stadium this summer - including to the stands and a new pitch which has been laid - as factors that make a possible agreement with Bath feasible.

"This pitch is built in a way that it could handle that and recover very quickly [from rugby]," Couhig said.

"Our football team is the first priority tenant and we would make sure it is handled the right way."

He added that any money generated would be reinvested in the football team.

"Let's say we did something with Bath Rugby, then we'd be allowed additional money under the SCMP [salary cost management protocol] to spend on our football players," he said.

title: Lancs, Yorks, Durham & Notts reach One-Day Cup knockouts as Flintoff hits first ton
description: Leicestershire, Lancashire, Nottinghamshire, Middlesex, Yorkshire & Durham all qualify for the knockout stages of One-Day Cup.
fullText:
Lancashire, Yorkshire, Durham and Notts were the main beneficiaries as the One-Day Cup group stage came to a conclusion.

While Group A leaders Leicestershire and Group B leaders Middlesex were already through, the other four places up for grabs all got sorted - but not without some real drama and dashing batting.

Lancashire booked their place in the quarter-finals with an enormous win over Somerset at Taunton, thanks to the substantial batting contributions of the experienced Keaton Jennings and the exciting Rocky Flintoff.

They both hit tons as Lancashire posted their highest ever List A score of 443, while the third remaining Group A spot was eventually claimed by Nottinghamshire, who beat Surrey at the Oval having chased down 299 thanks largely to George Munsey, who hit a terrific 138.

Joe Cracknell's maiden white-ball hundred helped Middlesex round out the group, ensuring top spot and a home semi-final on Sunday - their first in List A cricket since 1990.

They were joined in qualification by Yorkshire and Durham as last year's winners Worcestershire narrowly bowed out.

Rocky Flintoff hits first professional century for Lancs

Lancashire piled on a staggering 443-6 from their 50 overs in their victory over Somerset at Taunton - a record-breaking total reached thanks in no small part to sizeable hundreds from Jennings and Flintoff.

Opener Jennings hit 156 from 127 balls at the top of the innings to set a ferocious pace as Lancashire posted their highest ever List A score - eclipsing the 406-9 effort against Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge in 2019.

Teenager Flintoff joined in the fun, firing 10 fours and seven sixes on his way to 123 from just 76 balls. There was even time for Jack Blatherwick's quick-fire cameo of 32 from just 10 balls.

Somerset struggled to cope with the intense scoreboard pressure from the off and found themselves 33-2 when Tom Aspinwall (4-42) removed openers Johnny Connell and Savin Perera.

Tom Lammonby, who racked up 547 runs in this competition, hit 68 more but Somerset were bowled out for 269 as Lancashire advanced.

Surrey openers Ryan Patel and Dom Sibley put on 175 for their side's first wicket as they took on Nottinghamshire at the Oval, but Munsey's knock in the chase proved decisive.

Sibley departed for 84 but Patel brought up his century in 91 balls to lay a platform for the hosts, but Nottinghamshire fought back to reduce Surrey to 298-8 following a notable spell from Dillon Pennington (4-54).

Notts lost openers Freddie McCann and Ben Martindale relatively cheaply, but Munsey (138 from 132 balls)) and captain Haseeb Hameed (51) restored control to the visitors' chase and put on 109 for the third wicket.

Kyle Verreynne's unbeaten 57 carried Nottinghamshire over the line.

At Rugby School, Warwickshire eased to a comfortable 87-run victory at the expense of Kent, although neither side will advance beyond Group A.

The Bears were bowled out for 263, a total they reached after Vansh Jani's destructive 98 - the second time he has posted a career-best List A knock in three days.

Matt Milnes (4-52) led the Kent charge to ensure Warwickshire were all out with 29 balls remaining of their innings, having been put in.

Kent found themselves 23-5 after Bears seamer Ethan Bamber (4-29) ran through the top order. There was admirable resistance from Ekansh Singh (40) and Grant Stewart (41), but Kent were bowled out for 176 with a third of their overs unused.

Northamptonshire found themselves 27-2 against Gloucestershire at Cheltenham College but 79 from captain Nathan McSweeney and 75 from George Bartlett stabilised the visitors' innings.

Dominic Leech helped to elevate the visitors up to 308 having been put in by their hosts when he added 35 before being bowled by Daaryoush Ahmed, who finished with figures of 4-56.

Openers James Bracey and Cameron Bancroft put on 99 to tee up Gloucestershire but they then found themselves 200-5 and still with plenty of work to do.

Ahmed (48) again proved key, this time with bat in hand, as he and Joseph Eckland (68 not out) steered Gloucestershire to their target.

Yorkshire secured second spot in Group B with a seven-wicket win over Essex to book a home quarter-final at York on Friday.

Captain Dom Bess (3-32) and seamer Ben Coad (3-22) helped bowl out already-eliminated Essex for 151 inside 41 overs.

The Tykes then slipped to 15-2, but a second first-team half-century for England Under-19s man Will Bennison, who hit 60 off 59 balls, helped the visitors to their sixth win in eight group matches with more than 18 overs to spare - and a second quarter-final place in successive seasons.

Durham gained third place in the group but not before some late dramatic twists against the holders Worcestershire at New Road.

Worcestershire won the game by 77 runs on the back of being bowled out for a competitive 291, thanks largely to Tom Taylor's quickfire 86.

Ben McKinney then plundered 82 from just 70 balls but when he was out with Durham on 141-6, they still needed a further 63 to be sure of finishing above the hosts in the group.

When three more wickets went down in eight balls for the addition of just five runs, at 199-9, Durham still needed five more to reach that initial target of 204. They got them but not long before being bowled out for 214.

Hampshire had their hopes of reaching the knockout stages for a fifth successive year ended by Derbyshire in a thriller at Southampton.

Martin Andersson made 125, his fourth hundred of the summer across all formats, enjoying century stands with Harry Came (62) and Brooke Guest (67) as Derbyshire totalled 317-5.

But former Hertfordshire player Andrew Neal then almost turned the game on its head in Hampshire's reply.

Coming to the crease at 134-6, with 183 still required, he smashed 10 sixes in a 63-ball 110, his maiden professional century at the age of 26, before being caught on the boundary edge with nine runs still needed as Hants were bowled out for 309, with 10 overs to spare.

James Cracknell shared a third-wicket partnership of 202 with Nathan Fernandes (92) as Middlesex recovered from losing two early wickets to post a formidable 354-8 as they cruised to a 92-run win over Sussex at Radlett.

Half-centuries by former Middlesex man John Simpson (65) and Oli Carter (58) enabled Sussex to mount a respectable reply, but they were dismissed for 262 to finish bottom of Group B with just one win.

title: Mount set to miss Man Utd's Dublin game with Leeds
description: Manchester United midfielder Mason Mount is expected to miss the club's penultimate pre-season encounter with Leeds at Croke Park.
fullText:
Manchester United midfielder Mason Mount is set to miss Wednesday's pre-season encounter with Leeds at Croke Park.

Mount was outstanding in United's first three pre-season games, operating in the number eight role, with new signing Andrey Santos just behind.

However, he was kicked on the foot in the early minutes of Saturday's draw with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Although head coach Michael Carrick said he took Mount off in the first half as a precaution, and the 27-year-old was walking freely when he made his way to the team coach after the game, it is understood he has not trained since and is unlikely to play against Leeds.

It is not known whether Mount will be available for Saturday's final pre-season game against Ruben Amorim's AC Milan in Wroclaw on Saturday.

England duo Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo have also trained this week, although it is not known whether Carrick will feel they have had sufficient time on the training pitch to feature against Leeds.

title: Ramsay-Peaty fifth in European Championships 100m final
description: Adam Ramsay-Peaty was beaten for the first time at a European Aquatics Championships as he finished fifth in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.
fullText:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty was beaten for the first time at a European Aquatics Championships as he finished fifth in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.

The 31-year-old, who has 16 European Championships golds, had previously never lost a heat, semi-final or final at the event.

Olympic champion Nicolo Martinenghi won the race in 58.58 seconds, with Ivan Kozhakin finishing second and Italy's Simone Cerasuolo third.

Ramsay-Peaty finished 0.01secs and one place ahead of Great Britain team-mate Filip Nowacki.

The three-time Olympic champion, who is the 100m breaststroke world record holder, said "nothing makes sense" after a disappointing Commonwealth Games last month, where he won two bronze medals.

His time of 59.10 in Paris was 0.55secs faster than at the Commonwealth Games, where he was beaten by 18-year-old Nowacki, who made history for Jersey by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke in Glasgow.

Ramsay-Peaty later took part in Great Britain's mixed 4x100m medley relay final, swimming an impressive split of 58.9 in the breaststroke leg, but the team finished fourth.

Elsewhere at the championships, Great Britain's Katie Shanahan dominated the 200m backstroke to win gold by 1.49secs with a time of two minutes 06.13secs.

The 22-year-old won silver in the same race at the 2022 European Aquatics Championships in Rome.

GB's Angharad Evans, 23, also claimed a new championship record in the women's 100m breaststroke semi-final with a time of 1:04.97.

title: Zhang shocks Zhao in final-ball respot at China Open
description: Zhang Anda shocked world number three Zhao Xintong with a thrilling 6-5 victory by potting a respotted black ball in round one of the China Open.
fullText:
Zhang Anda shocked world number three Zhao Xintong with a thrilling 6-5 victory by potting a respotted black ball in round one of the China Open.

Zhang, who was down 3-0 in frames, fought back to eventually lead 5-4.

However, last year's world champion Zhao forced a deciding frame that ended in dramatic fashion.

"Today was just my day," Zhang said. "I hope that I can go far [in this tournament], I don't want them [two pots of the black] again. I was too nervous."

Zhang, ranked 19th in the world, was in control at 57-0 up, but Zhao fought back to lead with both players on the black.

The black was eventually potted by Zhang to force a respot - used as a tie-breaker when a frame ends with the scores level - with the 34-year-old prevailing.

He will now face England's Chris Wakelin.

"I made far too many mistakes today and I probably didn't deserve to win," Zhao added.

"I had prepared well for coming to Shanxi this time, and I didn't expect to lose in the first round. I played too badly and there was nothing I could do about it."

World number five John Higgins also lost in the first round after he was defeated 6-4 by 2015 world champion Stuart Bingham.

title: Doku 'not against' journalist who criticised him at World Cup
description: Jeremy Doku says he is "not against" the journalist who criticised his plan to leave the Belgium camp during the World Cup to attend the birth of his first child.
fullText:
Jeremy Doku says he is "not against" the journalist who criticised his plan to leave the Belgium camp during the World Cup to attend the birth of his first child.

Doku's wife Shireen was due to give birth during the second week of July and he told Reuters, external before the start of the tournament he intended to leave the camp to be at the birth even if his side were still in contention.

But it brought fierce criticism from L'Equipe channel presenter France Pierron, who labelled a father "completely useless" at the time of their child's birth.

L'Equipe later apologised and said Pierron's comments were "very far removed" from its values. The presenter also apologised but was taken off air until the end of the season of her show.

Doku eventually missed Belgium's 0-0 draw against Iran in the group stage to fly back to the UK for the birth of his son, Praise.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, external, Doku said he understood why some people questioned the timing of events.

"There was a lot of noise of course," the Manchester City winger said.

"I can understand why people felt like maybe this was orchestrated because it was too perfect.

"I also saw the journalist speak about me and the situation and all the people getting at her. But I just wanted to use this video as well to really... pray over her.

"I don't want to come at her in a way that most people did. I don't want people to be too harsh on her. We don't know what she has experienced. It's her opinion.

"She got fired and all these things. I never want this for a person. I'm not against her. I'm not angry at her or anything. She just said her opinion."

Doku played 86 minutes of Belgium's opening 1-1 draw with Egypt in Group G of the World Cup before missing their next game, with his absence explained as illness.

A Belgium statement later said, external that the 24-year-old travelled to London to be with his wife "with the approval of and accompanied by one of our team doctors".

title: Jets' Stiggers in hospital after collapsing in practice
description: New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers is taken to hospital after collapsing during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
fullText:
New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers was taken to hospital by ambulance after collapsing during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Stiggers briefly lost consciousness on the sidelines during a training drill, prompting an immediate medical response that halted practice for more than 10 minutes.

Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said the 24-year-old was conscious and talking before he was carried off the field on a stretcher for further examination.

"He came to the sideline after a play and he actually fell out," Glenn told reporters.

"The good thing is he was conscious. He was able to talk. For the most part, he's good."

The phone call that made Briton an NFL trailblazer

NFL players want more grass fields after World Cup

Several Jets players took a knee near the sidelines, while some formed a prayer circle as their team-mate was receiving medical attention.

"It was very sad, very emotional," running back Breece Hall said. "You get on your knee and say a prayer for him and hope he's OK."

Glenn also praised the Jets' medical staff for their handling of the situation and said he planned to visit Stiggers in hospital.

The practice reportedly featured multiple fights between the two sides, with Stiggers having his helmet thrown down the field during a scuffle with Buccaneers' Luke Goedeke.

Stiggers has 35 tackles, two fumble recoveries and three passes defended in 29 games for the New York outfit.

The Jets will host the Buccaneers in their NFL pre-season opener at MetLife Stadium, New Jersey on Friday (00:00 BST, Saturday).

title: Jodar on verge of smashing record for fastest rise to top 10
description: The teenage Spaniard's rise to the top of tennis is set to be faster than the sport's modern greats
fullText:
Rafael Jodar is on the verge of breaking the record for the fastest rise to the top 10 in men's tennis history after beating Arthur Fils to reach the semi-final of the Canadian Open in Montreal.

The 19-year-old defeated Frenchman Fils 7-6 (7-5), 6-3 and is now 11th in the live ATP rankings.

Should the Spaniard win his semi-final against Brandon Nakashima, he would enter the top 10 - unless Ben Shelton also makes the final, in which case Jodar would require a victory against the American too.

The current record for the shortest time between reaching the top 100 and then making the top 10 belongs to Boris Becker, who managed it in 210 days aged 18 in 1985.

If Jodar achieves the feat in Canada, he will do so in just 140 days.

Even if the Spaniard can't quite make it over the line in this tournament, good performances at the upcoming Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati or at the US Open would still very likely be enough to break the record.

Jodar's exceptionally quick rise has far outstripped those of men's tennis' 21st century greats.

It took compatriot Carlos Alcaraz 336 days to move from the top 100 to the top 10, while Novak Djokovic managed it in 623.

Both Rafael Nadal and Jannik Sinner did it in 735 days, and Roger Federer in 973.

The record in women's tennis is 203 days, set by Jennifer Capriati in 1990 when she was only 14.

The win over Fils means Jodar has become the first teenager since Stefanos Tsitsipas in 2018 to reach the last eight in Montreal, and he is the first player born in 2006 or later to make a Masters 1000 semi-final.

He has one tour title to his name, winning the Grand Prix Hassan II in Marrakech, Morocco on clay earlier this year.

Jodar only became a full-time professional at the beginning of 2026, but his debut season has drawn major attention and widespread excitement.

He earned his first Grand Slam win on his debut at the Australian Open in January, before reaching the top 100 in the rankings on 30 March by making it to the third round of the Miami Open.

Jodar was in the top 50 by 20 April, having secured his first win over a top 10 player, beating Australia's Alex de Minaur in his home city Madrid.

His back-to-back quarter-final appearances in Rome and Madrid were the first by a teenager since Nadal 21 years prior.

He then made the quarter-finals of Roland Garros in June and was knocked out by eventual winner Alexander Zverev, before reaching the third round at Wimbledon.

His incredible record in his inaugural year on tour means most bookmakers have placed him among the top eight favourites to win the US Open in New York next month.

It was Nadal who inspired Jodar to take up tennis lessons as a child - he refers to his namesake as his idol, and Jodar's game is defined by an aggression not entirely dissimilar from Nadal's.

At 6ft 3in, he hits heavy, high-speed shots loaded with topspin from the baseline that are designed to force opponents into submission.

His serve is several miles per hour faster than the tour average and his attacking style means he is prone to taking risks on big points and in rallies.

His playing style is much more similar to the relentless hard-hitting of current world number one Sinner, than the playful variety of Alcaraz.

With both Sinner and Alcaraz currently out with injury, Jodar's rapid ascent could mean he announces himself as the pair's most serious long-term threat in the coming weeks.

title: Palace co-owner spoke to McNeil's partner before move
description: Crystal Palace co-owner and chairman Steve Parish contacts Dwight McNeil's partner before the midfielder's move to the club.
fullText:
Crystal Palace co-owner and chairman Steve Parish contacted Dwight McNeil's partner before the midfielder's move to the club on Tuesday.

McNeil has completed a move to Palace and signed a four-year contract in a swap deal that involved Brennan Johnson moving to Everton.

McNeil, 26, nearly moved to Selhurst Park in the January transfer window when Palace agreed a loan-to-buy deal.

That deal would have turned into a £20m permanent move, only for the transfer to fall through when the required paperwork could not be completed in time, even though McNeil had already passed a medical.

After the deal fell through, McNeil's partner Megan Sharpley was critical of Palace, writing on Instagram: "We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is.

"So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that's OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it's just part of the job?

"To have something promised to you, to have been dragged along on an emotional rollercoaster and to be toyed with until the final minute. For that to be torn away from you at the last second with absolutely no explanation has hurt more than I can say."

BBC Sport understands that Parish reached out to smooth things over before this week's deal was completed.

McNeil joined Everton from Burnley for £20m in July 2022 and scored 15 goals in 128 games for the Toffees.

Palace have won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Uefa Conference League in the last two seasons.

"The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It's something that I want to be a part of, so I'm really looking forward to getting started," McNeil said.

Parish said McNeil is "a player with proven ability in the Premier League".

Johnson signed for Palace in a £35m deal in January but struggled to find form and made 26 appearances in all competitions without scoring.

The Wales winger joined Tottenham Hotspur from Nottingham Forest for a fee in excess of £45m in 2023 and scored their winning goal in the Europa League final last May before moving to the Eagles.

title: GB's Glave and Azu claim European 100m one-two
description: Great Britain's Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu claim a sensational European 100m one-two for the hosts in Birmingham.
fullText:
Romell Glave declared "total domination" for Great Britain after leading team-mate Jeremiah Azu to a sensational European 100m one-two for the hosts, 24 hours after Amy Hunt's triumph in the women's event.

Glave made an international podium for the first time by winning 100m bronze at these championships in Rome two years ago, but the 26-year-old upgraded to gold with a dominant victory in 10.09 seconds in Birmingham.

Raising a finger to the sky in celebration, he became the sixth British man to win the European 100m title - and third in the past six editions after Zharnel Hughes (2018) and James Dasaolu (2014).

Azu, the world and European champion over 60m indoors in 2025, improved on his 2022 bronze as he followed his team-mate over the line in 10.16 to the delight of the home crowd at Alexander Stadium.

German Owen Ansah completed the podium after Italy's two-time defending champion Lamont Marcell Jacobs pulled up with an injury at halfway.

GB's Hunt comes of age with European 100m gold

The team behind Hodgkinson's golden rise and the hunt for a world record

Three British men had qualified for the final, but Louie Hinchliffe did not contest the medal race.

"Upgrading from a bronze medal from 2024 is an amazing feeling," Glave told BBC Sport.

"The aim was to get [British] one, two, and three, but we got one-two, which is also amazing.

"I was ready for this occasion. The last week or so has been up and down with my body, but I was able to come out here regardless of how I was feeling.

On Great Britain's 100m performances, he added: "It is domination. Total domination."

Glave has made significant progress this season, breaking the 10-second barrier for the first time in legal conditions to win his first British title in June.

He has run sub-10 on six separate occasions, in all conditions, this season - including when he defeated the in-form Jacobs, a surprise Olympic champion five years ago, on his home turf in Italy.

That confidence was evident as Glave dominated his semi-final earlier in the evening, and he executed to perfection when it mattered most.

A talented junior, Glave was the fastest 17-year-old in the world in 2017 after he recorded a time of 10.21.

His progress has been disrupted by injury setbacks since, including a fracture in his back.

But, able to remain consistent with his training this year, Glave captured the gold medal he believed he was capable of winning two years ago.

The foundations of Glave's recent progress has come from a focus on sharpening the first 40 metres of his race.

After hitting the front by the 30-metre mark, he never looked back - and continued running far beyond the finish line in celebration.

After a golden 2025 season, Azu had finished fourth and fifth respectively at this year's World Indoor Championships and Commonwealth Games, with a season's best of 10.00 in Glasgow two weeks ago not proving to be enough.

While it was not gold in Birmingham, the 25-year-old was delighted to secure his return to an international podium following what he described as a "tough year".

"The most irregular [season] in terms of races, quite inconsistent," Azu said.

"When it comes to championships, I know I find my best. We always say times are irrelevant at this point. You want to go out there and race for medals.

"I want to put in my best performance in the final and I felt like I did that today. You always want to be on the podium. In the 100m there are over 100 guys that are competitive, so it is always tough."

There was a fifth-place finish for Hannah Nuttall in the women's 5,000m, as Italy's Nadia Battocletti retained her title.

Matthew Hudson-Smith, who has a stand named after him at the stadium where he trained as a junior for the duration of the championships, qualified for Wednesday's men's 400m final - although he had to settle for second place in his heat.

"I misjudged it a little bit. I thought I was clear," Hudson-Smith said.

"I was looking at the screen and I saw the guy try and surge. But he ran a PB, so he's messed up with the final ahead."

Elsewhere, Nadine Visser clinched the women's 100m hurdles by one thousandth of a second, with a photo finish required to separate the Dutch athlete and Poland's Pia Skrzyszowska.

title: Jaissle 'bit scared' how refs will take 'emotional' touchline style
description: Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle cut a measured figure at his unveiling news conference, but Premier League managers will come up against someone very different
fullText:
It was an unveiling that started with a handshake.

But no one needed reminding that Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle might not be quite so friendly in the coming weeks and months.

"Just the first time, guys," he said as he greeted reporters inside the media suite at St James' Park.

Jaissle, wearing a black suit and grey shirt, cut a measured figure throughout his first extended news conference since taking charge of the club earlier this month.

But Premier League managers will come up against someone very different on the touchline.

Those who know Jaissle best even liken the difference between his on and off the field persona to Jekyll and Hyde.

"I will not change my style because that's my personality," the former Al-Ahli and RB Salzburg manager said.

"On the touchline, I am emotional, but I need to respect the box [technical area] a bit more.

"I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little. I need to learn that.

"I had a long touchline in Saudi Arabia, so I think the GPS would be quite high if I had worn it!"

Such fervour was evident even as a player.

Jaissle's first career was ended by a serious knee injury at the age of just 25, but his intense desire to succeed has been a constant as former Hoffenheim team-mate Chinedu Obasi explained.

"Matthias has always been very hungry," he said. "He's had that leadership style and been vocal and passionate about the game. He wanted to win."

Predecessor Eddie Howe shared similar traits, of course, ending Newcastle's long wait for silverware by winning the EFL Cup in 2025 and qualifying for the Champions League twice.

Howe quickly recognised the importance of creating an environment at St James' Park where players felt safe, in order to play their best football, and he united the crowd following his appointment nearly five years ago.

There were a host of statement victories on Tyneside during his reign, but this one-time fortress started to crumble in the second half of last season as Newcastle finished in 12th place in the Premier League.

Newcastle's awful away form was well-documented in Howe's final campaign, before he stepped down last month, but they also lost seven top-flight fixtures on home soil.

Making the ground a difficult place for the opposition again will be among Jaissle's priorities after the 38-year-old and his staff were shown around for the first time.

"We were just looking at each other with a big smile, goosebumps," he said. "Just really special.

"The guys here who were leading the tour told me how it feels when the crowd are there.

"When we hopefully play in the way they want to see us - intense football, a vertical approach, aggressive, front-footed - there is a great synergy between the fans and the team."

The squad have become familiar with those principles following a draining training camp in Spain last week, which culminated in a 2-1 win against Valencia.

Goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek said Newcastle want to "show the opponents that they will have a hard time against us", while defender Malick Thiaw has spoken about the intensity under Jaissle being "really high".

Season ticket holder Adam Stoker feels the club still need further additions, but he believes Jaissle's playing style will be a "huge positive" as the German looks to build on Howe's legacy.

"Eddie did look a bit tired and didn't quite look the same manager as when he started," Stoker said. "Some of that energy had been lost and it correlated with the performances of the team.

"We have seen a tiny bit of Jaissle's ideas now and they seem to be very much in keeping with Newcastle in 2022-23, which was a hugely exciting team to watch.

"That playing style makes the crowd feel involved because the fans want to watch a high tempo.

"Playing front-foot, high-intensity football is something the crowd at Newcastle has always been on board with."

Jaissle now has little time to catch his breath before the season opener against Liverpool on Tyneside on 23 August.

This is a manager who, like all of the club's young signings this summer, has never experienced the Premier League before.

That brings the unknown, particularly after Newcastle lost key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes this summer, which Jaissle said has left a "vacuum".

But he also sees it as an opportunity.

"We are ambitious," he added. "That is the most important thing.

"It is why I decided to come here, but this will not happen overnight, especially when you have such a big transition phase now.

"You need to have a clear goal and wish of where we want to go to. That starts from the decision-makers, the management and the board.

"Then, if you have that synergy with the fans, the players and the staff to go there, I'm pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now."

title: Unhappy PSG given extra Super Cup dressing room
description: Champions League winners Paris St-Germain were unhappy with the space they were given at Red Bull Arena.
fullText:
Paris St-Germain have been given an extra dressing room for the Super Cup - after making their pre-game frustrations clear.

The Champions League holders were unhappy with their facilities at Red Bull Arena before Wednesday's Super Cup match with Europa League winners Aston Villa.

Unai Emery's side are using Red Bull Salzburg's home dressing room, leaving PSG with the away one in Austria.

But, at a pre-game meeting on Monday, PSG officials made Uefa aware they were not happy with the arrangements, feeling their dressing room was too small.

Sources told BBC Sport the French club wanted to be able to have the same size space as Villa, especially as they are the reigning Super Cup champions after beating Tottenham on penalties last year.

Uefa was able to allocate them a spare dressing room, normally used by the officials, to give them more space and the same as Villa. No officials were moved to accommodate Luis Enrique's side.

title: Super Giants deny Sunrisers and boost knockout bid
description: Manchester Super Giants gave themselves a huge chance of qualifying for the knockout stages of The Hundred with a 10-wicket win over Sunrisers Leeds.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Old Trafford

Sunrisers Leeds 127 (100 balls): Marsh 32 (23); Atkinson 3-30

Manchester Super Giants 128-0 (67 balls): Seifert 80* (40), Walter 44* (28)

Manchester Super Giants won by 10 wickets

Manchester Super Giants gave themselves a huge chance of qualifying for the knockout stages of The Hundred with a 10-wicket win over Sunrisers Leeds - denying their opponents an automatic place in the final in the process.

Set a modest 128 for victory, Super Giants romped to the total as Tim Seifert hammered an unbeaten 80 off 40 balls to secure victory with 33 balls to spare.

The result confirmed Trent Rockets' place at the top of the standings on 24 points and they go directly into Sunday's final at Lord's.

Super Giants, who managed to boost their net run-rate to 0.791 because of their margin of victory, are contenders to join them having moved above Sunrisers (0.603) into second.

Both teams in action on Tuesday can, in theory, can still be caught by Welsh Fire and MI London, who both play on Wednesday, but the latter two would have to win by substantial margins to increase their net run-rate totals of −1.001 and 0.262.

The teams finishing second and third play in the Eliminator at The Oval on Friday.

Despite the thrilling manner of Super Giants' chase, the principal factor behind this victory was a disciplined bowling and fielding performance after they asked Sunrisers to bat first on a batter-friendly surface at Old Trafford.

It looked a strange call when Mitch Marsh, the tournament's leading scorer, and Ryan Rickelton put on 42 in 22 balls for the first wicket.

But Noor Ahmad had Marsh caught for 32 at extra cover as he failed to convert his score into a match-defining one in what became a familiar pattern for Sunrisers as their middle order subsided.

Gus Atkinson snared the best figures for Super Giants with 3-30, but Sonny Baker struck at crucial moments to remove Zak Crawley (31) and Harry Brook (10).

The Sunrisers were eventually dismissed for 127 - their lowest total in this year's edition of The Hundred - with nine of their wickets out caught.

Super Giants then breezed to the target under the floodlights as Seifert and Paul Walter dismantled the Sunrisers attack with some explosive hitting.

The Kiwi smashed five fours and seven sixes as he and Walter, once again opening having been handed the role in Super Giants' recent win over Southern Brave, produced some destructive strokeplay.

Sunrisers had a glimmer when Seifert skied Abrar Ahmed on 57 but Crawley dropped a tough chance and the belief ebbed out of the visitors.

Any lingering hope disappeared entirely a couple of balls later when Walter - who made 44 not out off 28 balls - twice hammered Abrar for six down the ground.

It then became a matter of how much Super Giants could boost their net run-rate and, needing to win with at least 25 balls to spare to leapfrog the Sunrisers, they duly completed the job with ease.

Sunrisers hammer Super Giants to reach knockouts

The action switches to Sophia Gardens and Edgbaston on Wednesday with two double-headers as Welsh Fire host London Spirit while Birmingham Phoenix are at home to MI London.

Fire's women face Spirit at 11:30 BST while Phoenix play MI London at 15:00, although all four sides cannot make the knockout stages.

Fire's men still have hopes of making the Eliminator, though, but must win big against Spirit in their match at 15:00 to boost their net run-rate.

MI London need to do likewise in their fixture at Phoenix at 18:30 if they are to sneak into third place.
